optionRationales: Correct. AWS Step Functions it was specifically designed to orchestrate multi-stage workflows, coordinating calls to services such as Lambda. It allows you to configure 'Retry' (with configurable backoff) and 'Catch' (correction treatment including referral to compensation steps)) DECLARATIVAMENTE for each step, in addition to providing complete visibility of the state and history of each execution in the console — eliminating the need for orchestration logic and custom retry in the function Lambda orchestrator.

Incorrect as best approach. Chain invocations Lambda-for-Lambda directly creates a rigid coupling between the functions, hinders the visibility of the general state of the flow (there is no single panel showing at what stage each request is) and requires that CADA function implements its own logic of retry/error — exactly the complexity that the Step Functions solves centrally and declaratively.

Incorrect. Although the EventBridge be useful to uncouple components via events, it does not provide NATIVAMENTE configurable retreats by step of a NEGOCIO flow, nor a consolidated view of the state/historical of a specific end-to-end execution — central resources of the Step Functions for this scenario.

Incorrect. Combining everything into a monolithic function increases the execution time (and the risk of reaching the timeout of Lambda), makes it difficult to maintain/test independently of each step, and still does not solve the problem of FALTA OF VISIBILIDADE/RETOMADA in case of persistent failure — if the function fails in the middle, there is still no structured record of which stage was completed.

questions.text: An application uses a cluster Amazon ElasiCache for Redis with a primary node and a replica node, in different AZs, to store session data. questions.text: A company hosts static files from its website (images, institutional videos) in a pocket Amazon S3, Distributed globally via Amazon CloudFront. questions.text: A row Amazon SQS Standard is consumed by a fleet of workers EC2: each worker receives a message, processes the corresponding request (process that usually takes up to 2 The team noted that occasionally, the MESMO request is processed DUAS VEZES by different workers, causing duplicate charges to customers. The investigation revealed that the 'Visibility Timeout' of the row is configured with the default value of 30 What change solves this duplicate processing problem?
options: Migration from SQS Standard for Amazon SNS, which guarantees unique delivery (exactly-once) by default.
Configure each worker to delete the message from the queue IMEDIATAMENTE when receiving it, before starting processing.
Increase row 'Visibility Timeout' to a value greater than the expected maximum processing time (ex.: 3-5 minutes), ensuring safety margin.

questions.explanation: Right. 'Visibility Timeout' determines how long a message RECEBIDA by a worker stays OCULTA for other consumers. If processing takes up to 2 minutes but the timeout is just 30 seconds, the message is back to visible (and can be delivered to another worker)) ANTES that the first worker finishes and excludes it — causing duplicate processing. Configuring the Visibility Timeout for a value greater than the maximum processing time (with margin of security) solves this problem.
questions.hint: Think of how the 'Visibility Timeout' needs to be longer than the actual processing time, so that the message does not become visible again to other workers before being deleted.
optionRationales: Right. 'Visibility Timeout' determines how long a message RECEBIDA by a worker stays OCULTA for other consumers. If processing takes up to 2 minutes but the timeout is just 30 seconds, the message is back to visible (and can be delivered to another worker)) ANTES that the first worker finishes and excludes it — causing duplicate processing. Configuring the Visibility Timeout for a value greater than the maximum processing time (with margin of security) solves this problem.

Incorrect. Reduce Visibility Timeout even more PIORA the problem: the message would be visible to other workers even more quickly during normal processing of 2 minutes, increasing (not reducing) duplicate processing frequency.

Incorrect. SNS is a publication service/ASSINATURA (pub/sub) for notifications, not a row with a consumption model equal to SQS, and would not solve the pattern of 'a worker processes, excludes when finishing' described; moreover, delivery exactly once is a feature of SQS FIFO, not SNS in general, and the correct fit for this scenario is the Visibility Timeout.

Incorrect and risky. Delete message ANTES to complete the processing means that if the worker fails/stops DURANTE the processing, the message would be PERDIDA (without a chance of reprocessing) — exchanging the duplicate processing problem with a risk of PERDA of applications, which is usually even more serious.

questions.text: A company owns 8 VPCs (one per development team) that need to communicate with each other and with a VPC shared services central (e.g. directory, monitoring). AWS Transit Gateway acts as a hub of central routing: each VPC connects to it through A SINGLE Annex, and the Transit Gateway manages the routing between all connected VPCs (hub-and-spoke model) through centralized route tables. This replaces the need for 28 dot-to-point peering connections for only 9 attachments, drastically simplifying management and reducing the risk of configuration errors, maintaining connectivity between all VPCs,.

optionRationales: Correct. AWS Transit Gateway acts as a hub of central routing: each VPC connects to it through A SINGLE Annex, and the Transit Gateway manages the routing between all connected VPCs (hub-and-spoke model) through centralized route tables. This replaces the need for 28 dot-to-point peering connections for only 9 attachments, drastically simplifying management and reducing the risk of configuration errors, maintaining connectivity between all VPCs,.

Site-to-Site VPN is designed to connect a network ON-PREMISES to one VPC of AWS through the public internet — it is not the appropriate mechanism (not the simplest or most performatic) to connect VPCs to one another within the own AWS, and would still face the same problem of point-to-point connection scale.

questions.text: A team set up so much a Security Group as one Network ACL for the sub-network where their instances reside EC2. questions.text: A company needs that instances EC2 in a private sub-network access the Amazon S3 without traffic running through the public internet. NAT Gateway in the public sub-network that the fora today use for other Internet access. What is the most recommended solution to maintain the traffic of S3 within the network AWS no use NAT?
options: Keep it NAT Gateway and set up a S3 Bucket Policy that restricts access only to the IP of NAT Gateway — this ensures that traffic is controlled without the need for a VPC Endpoint
Create a VPC Interface Endpoint (PrivateLink) for the S3 — is the same as the Gateway Endpoint but with support to DNS and more security features, always being preferable to Gateway Endpoint

Create a VPC Gateway Endpoint for the S3 and add a route in the private subnet route table pointing to this endpoint — traffic S3 will flow directly through the backbone of AWS, without passing through NAT Gateway or on the Internet
Create a route to the CIDR of the S3 no IGW (Internet Gateway) of VPC, without passing through NAT Gateway
questions.explanation: Right. VPC Gateway Endpoint for S3 (or DynamoDB) is a router feature that allows for instances in private sub-networks to access these services via the internal network of the AWS. By adding the path 'pl-xxxxxx (S3 prefix list)' → Gateway Endpoint in the route table, traffic to S3 Stop going through the NAT Gateway and the public internet — safer and free of transfer costs via NAT.
questions.hint: Think about the type of VPC Endpoint that has no cost per hour and functions as a route table entry — designed specifically for S3 and DynamoDB.
optionRationales: Right. VPC Gateway Endpoint for S3 (or DynamoDB) is a router feature that allows for instances in private sub-networks to access these services via the internal network of the AWS. By adding the path 'pl-xxxxxx (S3 prefix list)' → Gateway Endpoint in the route table, traffic to S3 Stop going through the NAT Gateway and the public internet — safer and free of transfer costs via NAT.

Incorrect as an absolute statement. VPC Endpoint Interface for S3 (via PrivateLink) is a valid option and has specific advantages (such as accessibility via Direct Connect/VPN and support to more granular endpoint policies), but also has CUSTO per hour and per GB of processed data. For access of instances EC2 within VPC, the Gateway Endpoint to S3 is free and simpler — being the standard choice recommended for this case.

Incorrect for stated target. Configure bucket policy with IP of NAT Gateway still routes the traffic S3 PELO NAT Gateway and through the public internet, generating processing costs of NAT and keeping traffic out of the private network of AWS. The goal was EVITAR the Internet — a VPC Endpoint is the right solution.

Incorrect. CIDR of the S3 is a range of public IPs of AWS — add a route to these IPs in IGW it still involves the public internet, besides that instances in private sub-networks usually do not have direct route to IGW (this route exists in public sub-networks). This does not meet the objective of keeping traffic within the network. AWS.

questions.text: A company uses Amazon Macie to protect data in S3. The Macie reported that a bucket contains files with PII (names, CPFs, card numbers). The security team wants to be alerted in real time whenever Macie generate a new discovery of high severity, so that they can act immediately. What integration allows this with the least effort of configuration?
options: Configure the Amazon Macie to export discoveries to a pocket S3 and create a script that polling the bucket S3 periodically to verify new discoveries of high severity

Configure the Amazon Macie to publish discoveries no Amazon EventBridge — create a rule EventBridge that filters high-severity discoveries and triggers a topic SNS (sending email/SMS time) or a function Lambda for automatic repair
Create a AWS Config Rule managed by Macie which detects PII and shoot one SNS topic for immediate notification
Enable AWS Security Hub and create a custom filter for discovery of Macie High-Severity — Security Hub will automatically send an email to the team when the rule is activated
questions.explanation: Correct. Amazon Macie natively publishes all discoveries for the Amazon EventBridge in real time. A rule EventBridge with a filter by severity (HIGH/CRITICAL) can activate SNS for immediate notification, or Lambda for remediation — this native integration does not require polling and is the approach of less configuration effort recommended by AWS.
questions.hint: The Macie publishes discoveries in which local event bus AWS allowing real-time routing to multiple destinations?
optionRationales: Correct. Amazon Macie natively publishes all discoveries for the Amazon EventBridge in real time. A rule EventBridge with a filter by severity (HIGH/CRITICAL) can activate SNS for immediate notification, or Lambda for remediation — this native integration does not require polling and is the approach of less configuration effort recommended by AWS.

Incorrect. Although the Macie can integrate with the Security Hub (sending discoveries for consolidation), the Security Hub itself DOES NOT send emails automatically. For notifications, it would still be necessary to create a rule EventBridge in Security Hub or a custom action — it's no simpler than using EventBridge directly from Macie.

Incorrect as a less effortful approach. Do periodic polling of a bucket S3 introduces latency (not in real time), requires maintenance of script and scheduling infrastructure, besides being more complex. EventBridge is the recommended and simplest way for real-time alerts.

Incorrect. AWS Config evaluates the conformity of resource configuration (such as 'does this pocket have enabled encryption?'), does not analyze the CONTENT of objects S3 in search of PII. The Macie is the specific service for discovery of sensitive data in content — and the correct integration for real-time alerts is via EventBridge, no Config.

questions.text: A web application receives traffic from legitimate customers around the world. The security team has detected that a botnet is generating requests from hundreds of different IPs, but each IP makes few requests per minute (under any reasonable rate-limiting threshold per IP). The attack vector uses user-agent variation and does not make repeated requests to the same resource. AWS WAF is more suitable to detect and mitigate this distributed bot traffic pattern?
options: AWS Shield Advanced with Layer 7 DDoS protection enabled — automatically detects botnet patterns and creates rules WAF dynamics for each attack

AWS WAF Bot Control — a managed rule that analyzes bot behavior patterns (not just by IP or rate), using browser heuristics and telemetry signals to identify and block automated traffic, even if distributed in many IPs with few requests each
Rate-based rule no AWS WAF with a limit of 100 requests by 5 minutes per IP — by decreasing the threshold, the WAF block any IP that exceeds that limit, even those of the botnet
AWS WAF with rules based on geolocation blocking the regions where botnet operates
questions.explanation: Correct. AWS WAF Bot Control is a group of rules specifically managed to identify bot traffic — it goes beyond simple IP limits and analyzes behavior patterns, browser fingerprints, session anomalies and other heuristics. It is designed for distributed bots that avoid rate-based rules thresholds by IP.
questions.hint: When a bot attack distributes the volume on many IPs to avoid rate-limits, which rule managed from WAF analyzes behavioral patterns instead of just volume per IP?
optionRationales: Correct. AWS WAF Bot Control is a group of rules specifically managed to identify bot traffic — it goes beyond simple IP limits and analyzes behavior patterns, browser fingerprints, session anomalies and other heuristics. It is designed for distributed bots that avoid rate-based rules thresholds by IP.

Incorrect for this specific scenario. The statement describes a botnet where CADA IP makes few requests (under any reasonable threshold) — lowering the Threshold much would also block legitimate IPs from real users who make some requests per minute, generating false unacceptable positives. Rate-based IP rules are not effective against bots distributed with low volume IP behavior.

Incorrect. AWS Shield Advanced protects against volumetric and state DDoS attacks (Layer 3/4 mainly), with some support to Layer 7. However, he does not have the heuristics of individual bot behavior analysis that the WAF Bot Control offers for the described pattern (IPs with low volume, user-agent varied). Shield Advanced is more focused on mitigating volume peaks, not stealth bot traffic.

Incorrect. A globally distributed botnet usually uses IPs from many countries — including countries with legitimate users. Blocking geographical regions would cause legitimate users from the same regions to be blocked and would not solve the problem if the botnet uses proxies or IPs from regions that cannot be blocked (as the business country itself).

questions.text: A company uses Amazon CloudWatch Logs to store application logs, including records that may contain user personal data (names, addresses, IDs). The legal team determined that records related to a specific user should be permanently removed from CloudWatch Logs when it requests data deletion. What approach meets this technical requirement in CloudWatch Logs?
options: Enable encryption KMS in the Log Group and delete the key KMS corresponding to user data, making the logs unrecoverable
Export the logs to S3 with S3 Object Lock in compliance mode — data is protected against exclusion and privacy requirement is met by isolation
Use API CloudWatch Logs FilterLogEvents to identify logs streams and events containing user data and then use the API DeleteLogEvents (or DeleteLogStream) to remove these specific Log Group records
Configure a retention policy 1 day in the Log Group — so user logs will automatically expire in 24 hours, taking into account the exclusion requirement
questions.explanation: Correct. CloudWatch Logs offers the FilterLogEvents APIs (to locate events by default) and delete operations for streams and events. The correct approach to meet 'right to forget' requests is: locate streams/events with user data via filter, and delete specific events (via DeleteLogEvents) or the entire stream (via DeleteLogStream) as needed.
questions.hint: Think of which APIs of CloudWatch Logs allow you to identify specific events by default and exclude them granularly — without affecting other users' logs.
optionRationales: Correct. CloudWatch Logs offers the FilterLogEvents APIs (to locate events by default) and delete operations for streams and events. The correct approach to meet 'right to forget' requests is: locate streams/events with user data via filter, and delete specific events (via DeleteLogEvents) or the entire stream (via DeleteLogStream) as needed.

Incorrect. Reduce retention to 1 deleterious day TODOS the logs after 24 hours, impairing the operational diagnostic and audit capacity for TODOS the users. Furthermore, does not respond to an immediate request for data deletion from a specific user — the data would remain for up to 24 hours after request.

Incorrect. S3 Object Lock in conformity mode IMPEDE exclusion — is exactly the opposite of what the requirement requires. Object Lock is used for retention cases. WORM (write-once-read-many), not to facilitate data deletion according to privacy requests.

Incorrect. Delete a key KMS is a destructive and irreversible operation that would make TODOS the encrypted logs with that unrecoverable key — not just those of the user in question. KMS have a minimum waiting period (7-30 days) before effective exclusion, and the cost and operational risk are very high for this purpose.

questions.text: A security team uses the AWS IAM Access Analyzer to monitor external access to account resources. Access Analyzer created a discovery (finding) for a pocket S3 with a bucket policy that grants read access to another account AWS The team knows that this access is intentional and legitimate. How should they treat this discovery so that it does not continue to appear as an active alert, without removing permission?
options: Temporaryly remove Bucket permission, wait for Access Analyzer to reprocess and remove the finding, and then restore permission — Access Analyzer will not generate new finding for pre-existing permissions already processed

File the discovery in IAM Access Analyzer (Archive Finding), indicating that external access has been reviewed and is intentional — the discovery will remain in the state 'Archived' and will not generate new alerts, while the bucket policy remains unchanged
Delete Discovery (Delete Finding) IAM Access Analyzer — it will be permanently removed and will not even reappear if the Bucket policy is changed in the future

Add external account to 'IAM Access Analyzer Trust Zone' in account settings — any account access within the trust zone will not generate active finding, and the existing discovery will be automatically resolved
questions.explanation: Correct. IAM Access Analyzer allows you to archive finding (Archive Finding) to indicate that external access has been reviewed and is intentional — the discovery changes from 'Active' to 'Archived'. In addition, it is possible to add this account to the Access Analyzer's 'Trusted Accounts' (zone of trust) so that accesses from this account do not automatically generate new finding in the future.
questions.hint: The IAM Access Analyzer has a specific state for revised and approved discoveries as intentional — what is that state, distinct from 'Active' and 'Resolved''?
optionRationales: Correct. IAM Access Analyzer allows you to archive finding (Archive Finding) to indicate that external access has been reviewed and is intentional — the discovery changes from 'Active' to 'Archived'. In addition, it is possible to add this account to the Access Analyzer's 'Trusted Accounts' (zone of trust) so that accesses from this account do not automatically generate new finding in the future.

Incorrect. IAM Access Analyzer does not have an option to permanently exclude active access finding. Archived Findings remain in history. Furthermore, if the policy changes and external access continues, the analytics would generate a new finding — the previous 'Archived' state does not prevent this, but is the correct treatment for the current state.

Partially correct but inaccurate in implementation. Access Analyzer's 'zone of trust' is defined when the analytics is created (it can be the account or the entire organization). It is not possible to add individual external accounts to a 'trust zone' of an analytics after creation — you need to create an Organization Analyzer if you want to treat the entire organization as trusted. For specific accounts outside the organization, the correct is to file the finding.

Incorrect. Removing and restoring permission would only generate a finding again when Access Analyzer reprocessed the restored policy — because external access would re-exist. Access Analyzer does not 'memorize' old permissions — it analyzes the current state of policies.

questions.text: A company needs to ensure that all objects stored in a pocket S3 are encrypted, using specific keys KMS managed by the customer (SSE-KMS with a CMK The company wants to IMPEDIR that objects are stored without encryption or with the key KMS standard of AWS (aws/s3), but without blocking all written in the pocket. What is the correct implementation?
options: Bucket policy with Deny in s3:PutObject when the condition s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption-aws-kms-key-id does not match ARN of CMK specific, and also Deny when s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption is not 'aws:kms' — this forces the use of CMK correct
Create a policy of IAM which he denies kms:Encrypt for all identities except for the CMK specific — this prevents the use of other keys KMS no bucket
Enable SSE default encryption in the pocket with CMK specific — or S3 automatically apply correct encryption to all new objects, and no additional bucket policy is required to prevent other methods
Configure one AWS Config Rule that detects objects without correct encryption and uses automatic re-encryption to re-encrypt detected objects
questions.explanation: Correct. To force the use of a CMK specific to SSE-KMS, the bucket policy must have two conditions of Deny: (1) Deny when the cryptographic header isn't 'aws:kms' (blocking uploads without encryption or with SSE-S3/AES256), and (2) Deny when the key KMS not to CMK specific (blocking uploads that would use aws/s3 standard key instead of CMK). Both conditions together ensure that only the CMK correct to be used.
questions.hint: Think of two Deny conditions in the bucket policy: one to ensure that encryption is SSE-KMS, other to ensure that the CMK be the right one — not just one of them.
optionRationales: Correct. To force the use of a CMK specific to SSE-KMS, the bucket policy must have two conditions of Deny: (1) Deny when the cryptographic header isn't 'aws:kms' (blocking uploads without encryption or with SSE-S3/AES256), and (2) Deny when the key KMS not to CMK specific (blocking uploads that would use aws/s3 standard key instead of CMK). Both conditions together ensure that only the CMK correct to be used.

Incorrect as full control. The standard Bucket encryption applies SSE-KMS with the CMK configured when the client does NOT specify encryption on upload. However, if a client EXPLICITAMENTE send an object with SSE-S3 (AES256) or with a key KMS different, S3 IT WILL RESPECT the client's choice and overwrite the pattern. CMK specific without exception, a bucket policy is required with Deny.

Incorrect as preventive control. AWS Config is a control DETECTIVO and, at the most,, CORRETIVO (with SSM Automation for remediation). Incorrectly encrypted objects would still be ARMAZENADOS with the wrong encryption for some time before detection and re-encryption — does not prevent the incorrect recording in real time, as the bucket policy does.

Incorrect. A policy IAM which he denies kms:Encrypt for one CMK does not prevent the use of SSE-S3 (not using KMS). In addition, kms:Encrypt is not the action KMS used during upload SSE-KMS — o S3 use kms:GenerateDataKey in the name of uploading identity. The bucket policy with condition in the header S3 is the correct control to force the encryption method at the level of the pocket.

questions.text: A security team needs to have centralized visibility of security discoveries generated by multiple security services. AWS — GuardDuty, Inspector, Macie, Security Hub and AWS config — in a central audit account, without having to alternate between the consoles of each service individually. AWS was designed to add, normalize and correlate these discoveries in a single panel?
options: Amazon EventBridge with custom bus event rules collecting all security events from different services for a central target
AWS CloudWatch Dashboards customized with metrics from each security service, configured to show alerts in a unified panel
Amazon GuardDuty Aggregation with delegated administrator — automatically centralizes the discoveries of all multiple account security services

AWS Security Hub — adds, normalizes (for format AWS Security Finding Format - ASFF) and correlates discoveries of multiple services AWS Security (GuardDuty, Inspector, Macie, Config) and partners in a centralized vision, with support for multi-account organizations
questions.explanation: Correct. AWS Security Hub is specifically designed to be the 'single pane of glass' for security at AWS: aggregates finds of GuardDuty, Amazon Inspector, Amazon Macie, AWS Firewall Manager, AWS Config, and security partners; normalizes everyone in AWS Security Finding Format (ASFF); and offers a centralized dashboard with safety score based on CIS/AWS Foundational Security Best Practices.
questions.hint: What is the service of AWS acts as a single pane of glass for security discoveries, normalizing them in a common format and centralizing them with multiple services?
optionRationales: Correct. AWS Security Hub is specifically designed to be the 'single pane of glass' for security at AWS: aggregates finds of GuardDuty, Amazon Inspector, Amazon Macie, AWS Firewall Manager, AWS Config, and security partners; normalizes everyone in AWS Security Finding Format (ASFF); and offers a centralized dashboard with safety score based on CIS/AWS Foundational Security Best Practices.

Incorrect for this use case. EventBridge can centralize EVENTOS of services, but does not normalize finding for a common format, does not correlate with each other, and does not offer the security dashboard, compliance score or finding management that Security Hub provides. EventBridge is more suitable for response automation (activate Lambda, Step Functions), not for visualization and centralized management.

Incorrect. CloudWatch Dashboards show metrics and alarms, not security finding with context, severity, recommended remediation and life cycle management of discoveries. Creating dashboards that replicate the functionality of Security Hub would be complex and without the automatic normalization between services that Security Hub natively offers.

Incorrect. GuardDuty has multi-account aggregation with managing director, but this only centralizes the discoveries of THEIR GuardDuty — does not add to the Inspector, Macie, config or other services. To add multiple security services finding in a single panel, Security Hub is the correct service.

questions.text: A company stores confidential documents in Amazon S3. Documents need to be protected against accidental or intentional exclusion by any user, including the account administrator AWS — during a mandatory regulatory retention period of 7 years. Once configured, this block cannot be removed even by the IT team during the period. S3 meets this requirement?
options: S3 Object Lock in governance mode (Governance Mode) with retention period 7 years — equivalent to the mode of conformity for purposes of regulatory compliance

S3 Object Lock in compliance mode (Compliance Mode) with retention period of 7 years — in compliance mode, NENHUM user, neither the root of the account, can delete or change the object until the expiration period, being inviolable by design
S3 Replication with Delete Replication deactivated — Objects excluded in the original pocket are retained in the destination pocket for the required period
S3 Versioning enabled with MFA Delete enabled — any exclusion requires a second authentication MFA, making the process safe enough for regulatory compliance of 7 years
questions.explanation: Correct. S3 Object Lock in compliance mode creates a lock that cannot be removed or shortened by NENHUMA identity — including root of account AWS. This makes it suitable for rigid regulatory requirements (ex.: SEC, FINRA) where retention WORM must be absolutely inviolable by the configured period.
questions.hint: There's a way in S3 Object Lock which is absolutely inviolable — neither the root of the account can bypass. What is it, and what differentiates it from the most flexible way?
optionRationales: Correct. S3 Object Lock in compliance mode creates a lock that cannot be removed or shortened by NENHUMA identity — including root of account AWS. This makes it suitable for rigid regulatory requirements (ex.: SEC, FINRA) where retention WORM must be absolutely inviolable by the configured period.

Incorrect. Governance Mode also prevents exclusion by common users, but PODE be circumvented by users with permission IAM s3:BypassGovernanceRetention — including administrators with this permission. For requirements where NENHUM user can bypass the lock (including administrators), the mode of CONFORMIDADE is what is necessary.

Incorrect. MFA Delete requires additional authentication to permanently delete versions, but still PERMITE the exclusion by whom the device has MFA — usually the account administrator. There is no inviolable time lock as Object Lock in compliance mode offers., MFA delete protects against accidental exclusion, does not necessarily meet regulatory requirements of absolute immutability for fixed period.

Incorrect. Disabling the replication of exclusions means that exclusions in the source bucket are not spread to the destination bucket — but the objects in the source can still be excluded, and a certain administrator could exclude objects in the destination too. This is not an inviolable lock — it is only a partial layer of protection, not a secured regulatory restraint mechanism.

questions.text: A company uses AWS Systems Manager Session Manager for remote access to instances EC2 The audit team wants to ensure that TODAS the interactive sessions opened via Session Manager are recorded in detail — including all the typed commands and their outputs — for forensic audit purposes. What configuration in Session Manager activates this detailed record?
options: Configure Session Manager to transmit session logs to Amazon CloudWatch Logs and/or Amazon S3 via the SSM Session Manager — this captures the full command and response history of each session, with encryption KMS optional
Configure VPC Flow Logs in the sub-network of instances — network flow logs will capture all bytes trafficd during sessions, including commands
Install Amazon Inspector in the instances to monitor all the processes executed via Session Manager and send activity reports to CloudWatch
Enable AWS CloudTrail to record calls from API of the SSM — o CloudTrail automatically capture the commands executed within each Session Manager session
questions.explanation: Correct. Session Manager offers session logging configuration in the Preferences of SSM, allowing sending session logs to CloudWatch Logs (for real-time research) and/or S3 (when enabled, each session has its full input/output recorded — including commands and answers — with encryption support KMS to protect the contents of the logs.
questions.hint: Where in the console of SSM you find the configuration to send the full session history (input/output) to CloudWatch Logs or S3?
optionRationales: Correct. Session Manager offers session logging configuration in the Preferences of SSM, allowing sending session logs to CloudWatch Logs (for real-time research) and/or S3 (when enabled, each session has its full input/output recorded — including commands and answers — with encryption support KMS to protect the contents of the logs.

Incorrect. CloudTrail records calls from API (as ssm:StartSession, ssm:TerminateSession), i.e., events of CONTROLE — when a session was started, by whom, what instance. CloudTrail DO NOT capture the content of the interactive sessions (digital commands and their outputs). To do this, session logging is required configured directly in Session Manager Preferences.

Incorrect. VPC Flow Logs record METADADOS Network flow (IPs of origin/destination, ports, bytes transmitted, protocol) — NOT the content (payload) of the connections. Entered commands and their responses are the payload of the session, which the Flow Logs do not register. Furthermore, the traffic of Session Manager is encrypted in transit, so even if Flow Logs captured payload, it would be unreadable.

Incorrect. Amazon Inspector is a vulnerability and compliance assessment service — it checks whether instances have known vulnerabilities, software non-conformities, or network exposure. It does NOT monitor interactive sessions in real time nor records commands executed via Session Manager.

questions.text: A company uses Amazon Route 53 and the AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) to host a website HTTPS. Security team needs to renew certificate SSL/TLS before it expires in 30 The certificate was issued by the ACM for a domain in an area hosted in the Route 53. What is the expected behavior of ACM for that certificate?
options: For certificates ACM provided through validation DNS with records CNAME no Route 53, o ACM automatically renews before maturity — the renewal process is transparent and does not require manual intervention, provided the records CNAME validation exist in the DNS
The ACM automatically renews only certificates linked to CloudFront — for certificates linked to ALB or API Gateway, renewal requires manual intervention
The ACM send a notification email to the domain owner 30 days before maturity, requesting manual approval for renewal — the administrator must click on 'Renew' in the email to start the process
The ACM does not automatically renew certificates — the administrator must access the console ACM, apply for a new certificate and re-associate it with the resources (ALB, CloudFront) before maturity
questions.explanation: Correct. Certificates provided by the ACM with validation DNS (CNAME Records not Route 53) renew AUTOMATICAMENTE for ACM before maturity, without any necessary manual action, as long as the records DNS validation still exist in the host area. ACM periodically verify the validity of the records CNAME and renews the certificate in advance when confirmed.
questions.hint: The key is in the certificate validation method ACM — DNS vs. e-mail — and which of them supports fully automatic renewal.
optionRationales: Correct. Certificates provided by the ACM with validation DNS (CNAME Records not Route 53) renew AUTOMATICAMENTE for ACM before maturity, without any necessary manual action, as long as the records DNS validation still exist in the host area. ACM periodically verify the validity of the records CNAME and renews the certificate in advance when confirmed.

Incorrect for certificates with validation DNS. This approval behavior via email applies to certificates with VALIDATION POR E-MAIL — not to certificates with validation DNS. For certificates with validation DNS and records CNAME in force, the renewal is fully automatic, without approval emails.

Incorrect. GERENCIADOS for ACM (issued by itself ACM, non-imported) have automatic renewal when validation is correctly configured and records DNS The flow of 'request new certificate and re-associate' is necessary for certificates IMPORTADOS no ACM (external CA certificates), not for those natively issued by ACM.

Incorrect. The automatic renewal of the ACM does not depend on the service to which the certificate is linked (CloudFront, ALB, API Gateway, etc.) — depends on the VALIDATION METHOD (DNS vs e-mail) and validation records are in effect. Certificates with validation DNS automatically renews independently of the associated resource.

questions.text: A company has a multi-tier application: front-end in EC2 in a public sub-network, back-end in EC2 in a private sub-network, and database RDS also in private sub-network. The team wants to set up Security Groups following the principle of the least privilege. Security Group for the database layer correctly implements this principle?
options: The database SG must have an inbound entry rule on the door 3306 with source being the ID of Security Group back-end layer (not a CIDR IP) — This ensures that only instances with that specific SG can access the bank, regardless of IP

The database SG must have all doors open with source 0.0.0.0/0, but protected by NACL of the sub-network blocking all external traffic — the in-depth defence is guaranteed by the combination NACL + SG
The database SG must have an entry rule on the door 3306 with source being the CIDR Back-end private sub-network — this restricts access to only this sub-network
The database SG must have an entry rule on the door 3306 with source being the CIDR of VPC the whole — this ensures that only resources within the VPC can access the bank
questions.explanation: Correct. Use the ID of Security Group (not one CIDR) as a source in a rule of SG is the implementation of less privilege: only instances that have that specific SG can access the bank. This is dynamic (even with auto-scaling altering IPs) and granular (does not expose the door to the whole sub-network)./VPC).
questions.hint: Think of the difference between using a CIDR Subnet/VPC as source versus use of an ID Security Group as source — and which is more granular and dynamic for multi-tier architectures.
optionRationales: Correct. Use the ID of Security Group (not one CIDR) as a source in a rule of SG is the implementation of less privilege: only instances that have that specific SG can access the bank. This is dynamic (even with auto-scaling altering IPs) and granular (does not expose the door to the whole sub-network)./VPC).

Incorrect for lack of granularity enough. Use the CIDR of the subnet allows QUALQUER In this sub-network (or any new future resource added to the sub-network) access the bank — not only back-end instances. By using the back-end layer SG ID as a source, access is restricted only to instances that have that specific SG, regardless of sub-network.

Incorrect. Use CIDR of VPC the principle of the lowest privilege — any remedy in QUALQUER sub-network of VPC could access the database. Access should be specifically restricted to the back-end layer, using the SG ID as a source for maximum granularity.

Incorrect. Open all doors in SG to 0.0.0.0/0 with unrestricted source completely violates the principle of the least privilege — the SG itself should be the restrictive control, not depend exclusively on the NACL. The correct approach is each layer have its own restrictive SG, and the NACL be an additional layer of defense (not the only control)).

questions.text: A company is setting up the AWS CloudTrail in an organization AWS The team wants a central security account to receive and store TODOS the logs of CloudTrail of TODAS the accounts of the organization, and that the daughter accounts can NOT disable or modify the trail.?
options: Create an Organization Trail in CloudTrail from the management account (or delegated administrator account), configured to send logs to a bucket S3 in the central security account — Organisation Trails are automatically created in all the accounts of the organisation and cannot be disabled by the child accounts
Use AWS Configure with a cloud-trail-enabled rule on all accounts via AWS Config Aggregator, with automatic remediation that recreates the trail if disabled
Create a SCP no AWS Organizations which he denies cloudtrail:DeleteTrail and cloudtrail:StopLogging on all child accounts, and keep track independent on each account

Create a default trail on each daughter account individually, configured to deliver logs on the same bucket S3 central account — centralised management is achieved by the common destination of the logs
questions.explanation: Right. An Organization Trail created in the management account (or delegated audit account) automatically applies to all the organization's accounts. Daughter accounts see the trail on your console of CloudTrail as read-only — cannot disable, modify or delete it. Logs of all accounts are delivered centrally to the pocket S3 set up in the central account.
questions.hint: There's a kind of trail in the CloudTrail which is created once in the management account and applies automatically to the entire organization, being only read for the daughter accounts.
optionRationales: Right. An Organization Trail created in the management account (or delegated audit account) automatically applies to all the organization's accounts. Daughter accounts see the trail on your console of CloudTrail as read-only — cannot disable, modify or delete it. Logs of all accounts are delivered centrally to the pocket S3 set up in the central account.

Incorrect for the non-modification requirement. Trails created individually in each account are controlled by the administrator of each account — they may be disabled, modified or deleted by those who have permission in the child account. Organization Trail is the mechanism that prevents modification by child accounts.

Incorrect as a primary approach. AWS Config with automatic repair is a control REATIVO (detect and correct after the trail is disabled) — there is a time window where the logging would be interrupted. An Organization Trail is PREVENTIVO: daughter accounts simply do not have permission to disable the trail managed by the organization.

Incorrect as a solution COMPLETA. ♪ Out of the way SCPs with Deny for DeleteTrail/StopLogging protect existing trails from being disabled, this would require creating and maintaining trails in CADA It counts individually — a much more laborious operational process than an Organization Trail that automatically spreads. Organization Trail is the integrated and recommended solution.

questions.text: A web application receives calls from a function Lambda that needs to take on a IAM Roll to another account AWS (production account) to record metrics in a pocket S3. The roll in the production account has a trust policy. In addition to the trust policy of the destination roll, what is more necessary for the function Lambda manage to successfully assume the role via sts:AssumeRole?
options: A IAM Role of the function Lambda (in the account of origin) must have a policy that allows sts:AssumeRole to the ARN of the destination roll — both accounts need to authorise the operation: the destination account via trust policy, and the origin account via the policy of the roll Lambda

Only the trust policy of the destination roll is required — if it lists the origin account as entrusted principal, the function Lambda can automatically assume the role without any additional policy in the account of origin
The function Lambda needs a VPC peering configured with the production account so that the traffic of sts:AssumeRole crosses the network correctly between the accounts

The Bucket S3 in the production account you need to have a pocket policy that allows direct access to the role Lambda of the account of origin — the trust policy in the production roll is unnecessary in this case
questions.explanation: Right. For cross-account assumes role, authorization is bilateral: (1) a ROLE OF DESTINO need to have a trust policy that allows the account/roll of origin to assume it (mainly with the ARN the account or roll of origin), and (2) a ROLE DA LAMBDA (the account of origin) need to have a policy that explicitly allows sts:AssumeRole for the ARN Without both, the operation fails..
questions.hint: Cross-account AssumeRole requires bilateral authorisation: o DESTINO authorizes via trust policy, and ORIGEM You need what to allow your roll to make the call?
optionRationales: Right. For cross-account assumes role, authorization is bilateral: (1) a ROLE OF DESTINO need to have a trust policy that allows the account/roll of origin to assume it (mainly with the ARN the account or roll of origin), and (2) a ROLE DA LAMBDA (the account of origin) need to have a policy that explicitly allows sts:AssumeRole for the ARN Without both, the operation fails..

Incorrect. The trust policy of the destination roll is necessary but not enough. IAM Role used Lambda (in the account of origin) also needs to have a policy IAM explicitly granting sts:AssumeRole to the ARN without this policy in the origin account, the so-called sts:AssumeRole will be denied due to lack of permission in the calling identity.

Incorrect. Bucket policy allows access DIRETO to S3 without having to take another role — but the scenario specifies the use of sts:AssumeRole (taking a role in the production account). These are two different cross-account access mechanisms. For the flow via AssumeRole, the assumed role policy and trust policy are required — the original account policy is not sufficient.

Incorrect. AWS STS (Security Token Service) is a public service accessed via endpoints HTTPS — does not require VPC The call sts:AssumeRole is a call from API running via internet/endpoints AWS normally, independent of network peering.

questions.text: A company wants to encrypt data in transit between an instance EC2 and a cluster Amazon ElastiCache to Redis. Security team verified that the current connection uses the door 6379 no TLS. What change is needed to enable transit encryption in ElastiCache to Redis?
options: Configure a Security Group with rules that force the use of door 6380 instead of 6379 — ElastiCache automatically activates TLS when the connection uses the door 6380

Create a new ElastiCache cluster for Redis with 'In-Transit Encryption'' (TLS) enabled — this parameter can only be defined when creating the cluster, cannot be enabled in an existing cluster without replacement; the application must use the endpoint TLS at the door 6380 (or configured)

Modify the existing ElastiCache cluster on the console AWS enabling 'In-Transit Encryption' in advanced settings — the change will be applied during the next maintenance window without needing to recreate the cluster
Installing the agent AWS Certificate Manager in the fora EC2 — o ACM automatically manages encryption of all connections with services AWS managed as ElastiCache
questions.explanation: Correct. Encryption in transit in ElastiCache for Redis should be enabled at the time of cluster creation — it is not possible to enable or disable in an already existing cluster without creating a new one. When enabled, the application should connect using TLS, typically on the door 6380 (instead of 6379), and the ElastiCache certificate must be validated by the customer.
questions.hint: Remember: In-Transit Encryption in ElastiCache is a configuration that cannot be modified after cluster creation — what is the implication of this to enable TLS?
optionRationales: Correct. Encryption in transit in ElastiCache for Redis should be enabled at the time of cluster creation — it is not possible to enable or disable in an already existing cluster without creating a new one. When enabled, the application should connect using TLS, typically on the door 6380 (instead of 6379), and the ElastiCache certificate must be validated by the customer.

Incorrect. The In-Transit Encryption configuration in ElastiCache for Redis is IMPUTABLE after cluster creation — there is no option to 'modify' this configuration in an existing cluster. To enable TLS, it is necessary to create a new cluster TLS activated, migrate data, and update the application to the new endpoint.

Incorrect. The used door does not determine whether TLS is active — TLS must be explicitly enabled in the cluster. Security Groups control which IPs/ports can CONECTAR, But they don't activate TLS in communication. Security Group Locking the door 6379 and releasing 6380 It would only prevent connections at the wrong door — it would not guarantee TLS automatically.

Incorrect. AWS Certificate Manager certified management SSL/TLS for resources such as ALB, CloudFront, API Gateway — No Agent ACM' which encrypts arbitrary connections with ElastiCache. TLS in ElastiCache is a configuration of the service itself, activated in the creation of the cluster, and the application is responsible for using a client TLS compatible.

questions.text: A development team uses an account AWS shared for various environments (dev, staging, production). The security team wants to ensure that resources tags environment ('Environment: prod') in the production resources are maintained correctly — no one should be able to create or modify resources in the 'prod' tag without approval, and no one should be able to remove environment tags from existing resources. AWS allows you to apply and manage tag-based policies for tagging governance?
options: AWS Configure with 'required-tags' and 'restricted-tags' rules — detects features without the correct tags and automatically reverses unauthorized tagging changes via auto repair
AWS IAM with police that allow actions 'ec2:CreateTags and 'ec2:DeleteTags' only for non-production environment tags, applied to all development users

AWS Organizations with Tag Policies — Tag policies that define mandatory/allowed key tags and values for account resources, can be applied via SCPs which use conditions IAM (aws:RequiredRegion, aws:ResourceTag etc.) to restrict tag-based actions
AWS Service Catalog with launch constraints that require the use of specific tags during resource provisioning — this ensures correct tags since creation
questions.explanation: Correct.. AWS Organizations supports Tag Policies that standardize the use of tags (capitalization, allowed values) throughout the organization. SCPs containing tag-based conditions (such as aws:ResourceTag, aws:RequestTag), it is possible to restrict who can create/modify/delete resources with certain environment tags, implementing tagging governance.
questions.hint: What kind of policy is there? AWS Organizations is specifically designed for tag governance — defining which keys/values are allowed in account resources?
optionRationales: Correct.. AWS Organizations supports Tag Policies that standardize the use of tags (capitalization, allowed values) throughout the organization. SCPs containing tag-based conditions (such as aws:ResourceTag, aws:RequestTag), it is possible to restrict who can create/modify/delete resources with certain environment tags, implementing tagging governance.

Partially correct but incomplete. AWS Config detects features without mandatory tags (control DETECTIVO), and with remediation can add tags. However, automatic remediation has latency — features with incorrect tags exist shortly before correction. PREVENIR that production resources are created/modified without tag-based authorization, SCPs with tag conditions (control PREVENTIVO) are more robust.

Partially correct for Resource CREATION via Service Catalog, but does not resolve tag modification control on existing resources nor protects created resources outside Service Catalog. Service Catalog is a good practice for creative governance, but is not enough as comprehensive Tagging control.

Incorrect as a centralized solution. Create policies IAM specific by service (ec2, rds, s3 etc.) to control tagging is possible but extremely laborious — each service has its own tagging actions (ec2:CreateTags, rds:AddTagsToResource, s3:PutBucketTagging etc.), and keeping these policies on a scale is unfeasible. Furthermore, this does not address governance at organizational level that Tag Policies + SCPs offer.

questions.text: A company has an instance EC2 with a volume EBS encrypted data using a Customer Managed Key (CMK) of the KMS. The administrator needs to share a snapshot of this volume with another account AWS so that they can create an analysis instance. What is the correct process to share encrypted snapshot?
options: Re-encrypt snapshot with a CMK different than having permission to share with the target account (via key policy), modify the snapshot sharing permissions to include the target account — in the target account, copy the snapshot re-encrypting with a CMK Before use of the destination account
Export volume to S3 using AWS Sync Data and share object S3 with the destination account — S3 does not have the restrictions of CMK cross-account of EBS
Share the original snapshot directly (encrypted with the CMK) with the destination account — KMS automatically grants access to the key to the destination account when the snapshot is shared
Describe snapshot before sharing — create a non-encrypted copy of snapshot and share it with the target account to avoid complexity of key management between accounts
questions.explanation: Correct. Encrypted snapshots with a CMK can be shared between accounts, but the CHAVE KMS used in encryption should be accessible by the destination account. The recommended process is: (1) in the account of origin, re-encrypt the snapshot with a CMK which is shared with the destination account (via key policy with the ARN of the destination account), (2) share snapshot with destination account, (3) in the target account, copy the snapshot re-encrypting with a CMK own account destination for key independence.
questions.hint: To share a snapshot EBS encrypted with another account, you need to ensure that the destination account can use the key KMS — what this implies in relation to the key policy?
optionRationales: Correct. Encrypted snapshots with a CMK can be shared between accounts, but the CHAVE KMS used in encryption should be accessible by the destination account. The recommended process is: (1) in the account of origin, re-encrypt the snapshot with a CMK which is shared with the destination account (via key policy with the ARN of the destination account), (2) share snapshot with destination account, (3) in the target account, copy the snapshot re-encrypting with a CMK own account destination for key independence.

Incorrect. Sharing the snapshot itself DOES NOT automatically give access to CMK to the destination account. CMK must be explicitly updated to allow the target account to use the key (kms:DescribeKey, kms:ReEncrypt, kms:CreateGrant) — Without this change in the key policy, the target account cannot access the shared snapshot, because it is encrypted with a key without access for them.

Incorrect for security breach. Creating an unencrypted copy for sharing exposes data at rest without protection — violates the security requirement that motivated the original encryption. The correct approach is to maintain encryption throughout the sharing process.

Incorrect. Export to S3 via Data Sync is a data migration operation, not snapshot sharing — the data would be exported in file format, not a snapshot EBS In addition, objects in the S3 encrypted with SSE-KMS have the same key sharing restrictions KMS between accounts.

questions.text: A company uses AWS GuardDuty and detected a finding 'UnauthorizedAccess:IAMUser/ConsoleLoginSuccess.B' — a successful login on the console of a IAM User from an IP address in a country that the user has never used before. The security team wants to automate the response: temporarily disable the user's credentials while investigating. What is the most efficient way to automate this response?
options: Enable integration of GuardDuty with the AWS Security Hub, which automatically disables user credentials when detecting unauthorized access finding without additional configuration

Create a rule in Amazon EventBridge that filters findings from GuardDuty of the type 'UnauthorizedAccess:IAMUser/ConsoleLoginSuccess.B' and activates a function Lambda Who calls iam:UpdateLoginProfile and iam:UpdateAccessKey to disable user credentials IAM reported
Create a IAM Policy with Deny in all actions, attach to suspect user via API, and remove after investigation
Configure the AWS GuardDuty Auto-Remediation — a native resource of GuardDuty which automatically blocks users IAM identified in high-risk finding
questions.explanation: Correct. GuardDuty publish findings automatically no Amazon EventBridge. A Rule EventBridge with filter in the specific kind of finding can trigger a Lambda of immediate response using the IAM API to: disable access to the console (UpdateLoginProfile or remove password), disable access keys (UpdateAccessKey with Status=Inactive), and notify the team. This automation responds in seconds without human intervention.
questions.hint: The GuardDuty generate real-time finding — which local event bus service receives these finding and can trigger response automations?
optionRationales: Correct. GuardDuty publish findings automatically no Amazon EventBridge. A Rule EventBridge with filter in the specific kind of finding can trigger a Lambda of immediate response using the IAM API to: disable access to the console (UpdateLoginProfile or remove password), disable access keys (UpdateAccessKey with Status=Inactive), and notify the team. This automation responds in seconds without human intervention.

Incorrect. AWS Security Hub aggregates and normalizes findings (centralization and visibility), but does not perform automatic remediation on its own. For automatic remediation, it is necessary to create rules EventBridge or Custom Actions at the Security Hub Lambda or Step Functions — Security Hub alone doesn't change credentials IAM.

Incorrect. GuardDuty has no native 'auto-remediation' resource that modifies credentials IAM. The GuardDuty is a DETECTION service (identifies threats and generates finding) — automatic remediation must be implemented by the user via EventBridge + Lambda (or AWS Systems Manager Automation).

Correct in the logic of blocking, but INCORRETO as an efficient automation approach integrated with GuardDuty. This approach required: knowing the user name of the finding, calling iam:AttachUserPolicy — what is more complex to implement than simply disable credentials (UpdateLoginProfile/UpdateAccessKey), which is the direct and reversible approach. EventBridge + Lambda to be automated, but with unnecessarily complex steps.

questions.text: A company needs to control which services and APIs can be called from within a VPC, even by IAM Roles with wide permissions — wanting to ensure that calls from API only possible for a limited set of services AWS when originating from the corporate network. IAM allows you to restrict permissions based on VPC or the origin endpoint of the call API?
options: Use the condition aws:RequiredRegion to limit calls from API only to the region where the VPC it is, ensuring that calls from outside the network do not reach services in the same region
Use the condition aws:MultiFactorAuthPresent to ensure that calls from API are only made after authentication MFA, which implicitly confirms that the user is on the corporate network
Use the condition aws:SourceIp with IPs range of NAT Gateway of the company — any call from API of the VPC will pass through the NAT Gateway, which has a fixed IP

Use the condition IAM aws:SourceVpc (for calls via VPC end point) or aws:SourceVpce (for a specific endpoint) in policies IAM or resource polices — these conditions allow to ensure that the call for API originating from a VPC or specific endpoint
questions.explanation: Correct. Conditions keys aws:Source aws:SourceVpce allows you to create policies that only allow calls from API when they originate from a VPC specific (or endpoint) VPC This is useful for endpointing policies of VPC endpoints (restricting which resources can be accessed) and for policy resource (restricting access from controlled sources)).
questions.hint: Which conditions are key IAM check the VPC or VPC source endpoint of a call from API — useful in endpoint police and resource police?
optionRationales: Correct. Conditions keys aws:Source aws:SourceVpce allows you to create policies that only allow calls from API when they originate from a VPC specific (or endpoint) VPC This is useful for endpointing policies of VPC endpoints (restricting which resources can be accessed) and for policy resource (restricting access from controlled sources)).

Incorrect and fragile. Using aws:SourceIp with IP of NAT Gateway, direct calls via VPC endpoints do not pass through NAT Gateway (and would have the IP of origin as the IP of the instance, not of the NAT) — the condition wouldn't work for those calls., aws:SourceIp does not work as expected for via calls VPC endpoints, because the reported IP can be the private IP, not the IP of the NAT.

Incorrect. aws:RequestedRegion limits the region where resources AWS are operated — does not identify ORIGEM of call (VPC vs internet). Even from outside the VPC corporate, someone could make calls to the same region using stolen credentials — this condition does not meet the goal of restricting by network origin.

Incorrect. aws:MultiFactorAuthPresent checks if MFA was used in authentication, not the REDE of origin. MFA can be used from anywhere — the condition does not guarantee that the call originates from the VPC corporate.

questions.text: A company needs external users (clients) B2C) authenticate in a web application using your social accounts (Google, Facebook) or an owner login. After authentication, the application needs to issue a JWT for the front-end use as Bearer token on calls to API REST. What service AWS manages this life cycle of external users and emission of tokens JWT with the least development effort?
options: AWS IAM Identity Center (SSO) — supports external identity providers and issues tokens JWT for web application front-ends B2C

Amazon Cognito User Pool — manage or register, login, MFA, federation with social providers (Google, Facebook via OIDC/SAML) and emits tokens JWT (ID token, Access token, Refresh token) standardized for use as Bearer token in APIs
Amazon Cognito Identity Pool (Federated Identity) — external user authentication management with social providers and issue tokens JWT for use as Bearer token
Amazon API Gateway with Lambda Custom Authorizer implementing OAuth 2.0 and emits tokens JWT — is the recommended approach when you need social federation and tokens JWT customised
questions.explanation: Correct. Amazon Cognito User Pool is the managed service of AWS specifically for user authentication (B2C or B2B), with native support to social identity providers (Google, Facebook, Amazon), federation SAML/OIDC, and emission of token JWT standard (ID Token, Access Token, Refresh Token). It is the solution of least development effort for this scenario.
questions.hint: Clearly separate: User Pool manages USERS and issues JWT Application; Identity Pool exchange tokens by CREDENCIAIS AWS. What is the scenario here — authentication of external users or direct access to resources AWS?
optionRationales: Correct. Amazon Cognito User Pool is the managed service of AWS specifically for user authentication (B2C or B2B), with native support to social identity providers (Google, Facebook, Amazon), federation SAML/OIDC, and emission of token JWT standard (ID Token, Access Token, Refresh Token). It is the solution of least development effort for this scenario.

Incorrect as to the primary purpose. Cognito Identity Pool receives tokens from identity providers (including Cognito User Pools) and the TROCA by credentials AWS temporary (via STS). It does not manage the life cycle of users (cassket, login), MFA), does not issue JWT how to Bearer tokens application — that's the role of User Pool.

Incorrect. IAM Identity Center is designed for WORKFORCE (employees, partners) access accounts AWS and integrated corporate applications — not for external users B2C applications. Not suitable for registration, login and external client identity management.

Incorrect as less effort approach. Implement OAuth 2.0 complete with social federation via Lambda Custom Authorizer is extremely laborious (manage OAuth flows, refresh tokens, MFA, register etc.) compared to Cognito User Pool, which offers all this as managed service with minimal configuration.

questions.text: An application uses AWS Lambda with access to a database. The database credentials are stored in AWS Secrets Manager. The team noticed that the function Lambda seeks the secret to each invocation, increasing latency and cost. How to optimize this pattern without sacrificing security or losing secret rotations?
options: Use AWS Secrets Manager with cache in Lambda a Secrets Manager caching library or o Lambda Extension to Secrets Manager — the secret is sought in the first invocation and cached in memory during the TTL configured; after the TTL, a new search occurs to capture rotations
Increase function timeout Lambda for 15 minutes, so that she keeps the connection to the bank open throughout the processing without having to search for the secret again

Store credentials in an environment variable of the Lambda, updating it manually after each rotation of the Secrets Manager — environment variables are encrypted by KMS and have better performance than calls to API

Configure the function Lambda to search for the secret only in the first invocation cold start (outside the handler, in the initialization code), storing in a global variable — hot executions (warm) will reuse the variable without further search
questions.explanation: Correct. AWS provides a cache library for Secrets Manager (for different languages) and a Lambda They keep the secret in memory by TTL configured (ex.: 5 minutes), doing a new search only when the cache expires — reducing calls to API of the Secrets Manager, latency by invocation, and cost, while still captures new credentials after rotations within the TTL.
questions.hint: A AWS offers specific tools for cache of secrets in Lambda — which allows to reuse credentials between invocations while still detects rotations after a TTL?
optionRationales: Correct. AWS provides a cache library for Secrets Manager (for different languages) and a Lambda They keep the secret in memory by TTL configured (ex.: 5 minutes), doing a new search only when the cache expires — reducing calls to API of the Secrets Manager, latency by invocation, and cost, while still captures new credentials after rotations within the TTL.

Incorrect for breaking the benefit of automatic rotation. Using environment variables with manual update eliminates the main benefit of Secrets Manager (automatic rotation without downtime). After a rotation, the credentials in the environment variables would be outdated until manual intervention, causing connection failures. Environment variables also remain in plain text in the context of execution after description, with less access control than the Secrets Manager.

Incorrect for loss of rotations. Store the secret out of the handler in a global variable means that it is cached indefinitely while the execution environment is heated (warm). After a credential rotation, the hot environments will continue to use the old credential indefinitely, causing connection errors to the bank that requires the new credential. TTL is the correct approach to balancing performance and rotation support.

Incorrect. Increasing the timeout of the function has no relation to the frequency of secret search — the additional latency comes from the call to API of the Secrets Manager not of the duration of the execution., Lambda is not designed for long executions with persistent bank connections — for this, the correct pattern would be RDS Proxy.

questions.text: A company needs developers to create and manage their own IAM Roles for test applications, but with a restriction: the roles created should never be able to access the pocket S3 Production (arn):aws:s3:::The administrator wants to delegate this freedom without opening the risk of escalating privileges for production data. IAM implements this 'cap' of permissions for the roles created by developers?
options: Boundary Permissions — the administrator creates a managed policy with Deny explicit for s3:* in the product-data resource and defines it as mandatory boundary permissions by granting developers permission to create roles, using condition IAM which requires the bondary in iam:CreateRole

Create a SCPs with a condition that checks whether the roll was created by a user of the developer group — any roll created by the developer automatically inherits the group restrictions, including without access to prod-data

IAM Policy with Deny for iam:CreateRole for any role that doesn't have a 'Environment: dev' tag — only dev roles can be created by developers, and dev roles can't access the prod-data pocket by company policy
SCP no AWS Organizations with Deny to s3:GetObject in the prod-data pocket for the OR of developers — this prevents developers' created roles from accessing the production pocket
questions.explanation: Right. Boundaries permissions are political. IAM which define the Maximum Permissions that an identity may have. The administrator may: (1) create a boundary policy permissions that excludes access to the production loop, (2) grant developers permission to iam:CreateRole but with the condition iam:PermissionsBoundary compulsory specifying this boundary. Thus, any roller created by the developer cannot, in practice, be allowed to access the prod-data bucket — even if the policy attached to the roller tries to grant.
questions.hint: What recourse? IAM defines the Maximum Roller Permissions — acting as a ceiling that even the policies attached to the roll cannot exceed?
optionRationales: Right. Boundaries permissions are political. IAM which define the Maximum Permissions that an identity may have. The administrator may: (1) create a boundary policy permissions that excludes access to the production loop, (2) grant developers permission to iam:CreateRole but with the condition iam:PermissionsBoundary compulsory specifying this boundary. Thus, any roller created by the developer cannot, in practice, be allowed to access the prod-data bucket — even if the policy attached to the roller tries to grant.

Partially correct but with a problem: SCPs apply to TODOS the resources in the account/OR, including legitimate production applications that may need to access the prod-data pocket in the same account. SCPs do not discriminate between roles created by developers and existing production roles — a SCP which denies access to the prod-data pocket for the whole OR could break production applications. Boundaries permissions are more surgical.

Incorrect. Tags are metadata — do not create technical permission restrictions. A developer with permission to create roles could simply create a role without the 'dev' tag, or with the 'dev' tag and then try to use the role to access prod-data (if the role itself has no access restriction). Tags are effective controls only when combined with policy conditions, and yet do not have the scope of the Boundary Permissions to restrict the maximum permission scope.

Incorrect. SCPs have no conditions based on 'who created the resource' (IAM roles do not have an attribute 'created by' that can be evaluated in SCP conditions). SCPs evaluate the current session (who is CHAMANDO a API), In addition, a role's permissions are not inherited from the creator — a new role has only the policies explicitly attached to it..

questions.text: A company has a legacy application in the local data center that needs to authenticate itself in the AWS to post messages in rows SQS, no possibility to use IAM Roles (because it's not an instance) EC2 nor Lambda). The security team wants to avoid the use of long-term key accesses. AWS allows the application to obtain temporary credentials without needing permanent key accesses?
options: AWS IAM Roles Anywhere — Allows Workloads Outside of AWS (on-premises, other clouds) change X certificates.509 of a reliable CA by credentials IAM temporary STS, eliminating the need for long-term static key accesses
Create a user IAM with long-term key accesses and store them in a secure password box (like HashiCorp Vault) — security is guaranteed by the safe protection, not by the credentials themselves

Configure a connection AWS Direct Connect from the company to AWS and use AWS STS with AssumeRole based on the IP of origin of the on-premises network — the dedicated private network eliminates the need for strong credentials
Use AWS Cognito Identity Pool with anonymous authentication (unauthenticated identities) to obtain credentials AWS temporary for legacy application, without the need for certificates or keys
questions.explanation: Correct. AWS IAM Roles Anywhere was created specifically for this case: allows applications outside the AWS (on-premises, other clouds) get credentials AWS temporary X-certificates.509 issued by a reliable CA (configured in Trust Anchor). The process changes the certificate to credentials STS temporary, eliminating static key accesses. The credentials are short-lived and can be rotated automatically via certificate renewal.
questions.hint: What service AWS was released to allow workloads out of AWS (on-premises) obtain temporary credentials by submitting X certificates.509, no static key accesses?
optionRationales: Correct. AWS IAM Roles Anywhere was created specifically for this case: allows applications outside the AWS (on-premises, other clouds) get credentials AWS temporary X-certificates.509 issued by a reliable CA (configured in Trust Anchor). The process changes the certificate to credentials STS temporary, eliminating static key accesses. The credentials are short-lived and can be rotated automatically via certificate renewal.

Incorrect for not meeting the requirement to remove long-term key accesses. Regardless of where they are stored, static key accesses have the risks associated with unlimited duration (do not automatically expire) and may be compromised if the vault is breached. The explicit requirement is to avoid long-term beliefs.

Incorrect. Direct Connect is a network connectivity solution — it is not a authentication mechanism. STS:TakeRole, the application would still need some initial credentials (access keys or other authentication mechanism) to make the call to STS. Direct Connect does not eliminate the need for credentials.

Incorrect. Unauthenticated identities of Cognito Identity Pool provide credentials with minimal permissions, typically for mobile/web applications from unidentified customers. Using anonymous authentication for a server application would be a security vulnerability — anyone could get those credentials, and the lower privilege policy would be difficult to apply specifically for that application.

questions.text: A company stores database passwords in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store using the SecureString type (encrypted with KMS). The team is evaluating whether to migrate to the AWS Secrets Manager. What's the difference MAIS RELEVANTE between the two services that would justify migration to the Secrets Manager specifically for database credentials?
options: The Secrets Manager offers automatic and managed database credentials rotation — with native integration with RDS, Redshift, DocumentDB to change the password in the bank and update the secret automatically, without manual intervention, using a Lambda of rotation managed by the AWS
The Secrets Manager has a lower cost per API call and secret stored, making it more economical for large volumes of secrets
The Secrets Manager has less latency when recovering secrets because it is a service dedicated to secrets, while the SSM Parameter Store has high latency because it is a multipurpose service
The Secrets Manager supports encryption KMS for secrets, while the SSM Parameter Store SecureString does not support encryption KMS with customer CMKs
questions.explanation: The automatic rotation of credentials is the most significant functional difference. Secrets Manager has native integration with database services AWS (RDS MySQL/PostgreSQL, Redshift, DocumentDB) for: (1) generate a new password, (2) update it in the database, (3) update the secret in Secrets Manager — all automatically in a configurable cycle. SSM Parameter Store does not have this built-in automatic rotation feature.
questions.hint: What functionality or Secrets Manager offers specifically for database credentials that the SSM Parameter Store SecureString doesn't have native?
optionRationales: The automatic rotation of credentials is the most significant functional difference. Secrets Manager has native integration with database services AWS (RDS MySQL/PostgreSQL, Redshift, DocumentDB) for: (1) generate a new password, (2) update it in the database, (3) update the secret in Secrets Manager — all automatically in a configurable cycle. SSM Parameter Store does not have this built-in automatic rotation feature.

Incorrect. The recovery latency between Secrets Manager and SSM Parameter Store (with caching) is comparable for typical use cases. The main distinction is not performance, but functionality — especially automatic rotation integrated with databases, that the Secrets Manager natively offers.
Incorrect. SSM Parameter Store SecureString SUPORTA Customer Managed Keys (CMKs) — you can specify a CMK specific when creating a SecureString parameter. Both services support KMS with customer CMKs.

Incorrect. In practice, Secrets Manager there's a cost. POR SEGREDO per month and per month API call — usually MAIS CARO than the SSM Parameter Store (which offers free storage of Standard parameters and low cost for Advanced). The justification for using Secrets Manager not cost, but functionality — especially automatic rotation.

questions.text: A company set up a AWS WAF in front of a Application Load Balancer. The security team wants to create a rule that specifically blocks requests where the User-Agent HTTP contains the string 'sqlmap' (a tool of SQL automated injection) anywhere in the header. What kind of rule WAF implements it directly?
options: String match rules no AWS WAF with type of inspection 'Contains' in the field 'Single Header' with name 'User-Agent' and string 'sqlmap' — this rule matches in any request where the User-Agent contains 'sqlmap' and applies the Block action
SQL injection match rule no AWS WAF, which automatically detects patterns of SQL injection into User-Agent and other fields, including identification of the sqlmap tool
Rate-based rule with very low threshold (ex.: 1 request by 5 minutes) for IPs with User-Agent containing 'sqlmap' — this effectively blocks attacks from the sqlmap that make many requests
