Use VPC Peering between the two regions — Peering routes the transfer of data through the backbone network of AWS, making cross-region transfer free
Use S3 Transfer Acceleration to reduce cross-region transfer costs — Transfer Acceleration uses the network of AWS instead of the public internet, reducing the cost per GB transferred

Move function Lambda (or the service that consumes the results of Athena) for the same region where the bucket S3 is — data transfer within the same region AWS between services is free, eliminating cross-region transfer costs
questions.explanation: Correct. Transfer of data between services AWS the MESMA REGION is free of charge (ex.: S3 → Lambda in the same region = $0). Cross-region transfer costs per GB. Move Lambda and other processing for the same region of S3 it eliminates these costs. It is a fundamental practice of architecture: keep data and compute in the same region to avoid transfer costs.
questions.hint: Transfer of data between services AWS within the MESMA And how does this compare to cross-region transfer??
optionRationales: Correct. Transfer of data between services AWS the MESMA REGION is free of charge (ex.: S3 → Lambda in the same region = $0). Cross-region transfer costs per GB. Move Lambda and other processing for the same region of S3 it eliminates these costs. It is a fundamental practice of architecture: keep data and compute in the same region to avoid transfer costs.

Incorrect. S3 Transfer Acceleration UPLOADS from end-users to S3 using edge locations of the CloudFront — does not reduce cross-region transfer costs between services AWS. In fact, Transfer Acceleration has cost ADICIONAL per GB in addition to the normal transfer cost. Not suitable for this case.

Incorrect as cost solution. Create a replica S3 in another region has replication cost (cross-region transfer to replicate data) + duplicate storage cost in the new region. AUMENTA the total cost instead of eliminating the transfer costs. Move processing to the region of the S3 It's much simpler and cheaper..

Incorrect. VPC Peering between regions (Inter-region VPC Peering) uses the backbone network of AWS but it's NOT free — it has GB data transfer cost similar to the standard cross-region. VPC Peering reduces latency and increases security (does not pass through the public internet), but does not eliminate cross-region transfer costs.

questions.text: A company has a database Amazon RDS MySQL is interrupted every night at 22h and restarted at 7h in the morning to save costs. 7 days stopped, the instance is automatically restarted and the team receives an unexpected recovery. Why the RDS is automatically restarted?
options: The CloudWatch has an alarm configured to restart the RDS if CPU stay below 0.1% for more than 7 days — this behavior is the standard and cannot be disabled

The Amazon RDS limits the time that an instance may remain standing 7 days — after that period, RDS automatically restarts the instance to ensure that patches and necessary maintenance can be applied; the team is normally charged after automatic reset
The RDS is restarted because the scheduled automatic backup happened during the stationary period — automated backups can only be done with the instance running, forcing the restart
The RDS automatically restarts when the standby Multi-AZ detects that the primary is inactive for more than 7 days and assumes the role of primary
questions.explanation: Correct. RDS has a limitation that stalled instances are automatically restarted after 7 days. This ensures that instances receive security patches and maintenance updates that can only be applied with the instance in execution. If the team does not plan the RDS to save inside 7 days, the instance is restarted automatically and the billing returns to normal.
questions.hint: The RDS it has a maximum time limit for an instance to remain stationary — after that period, which happens automatically?
optionRationales: Correct. RDS has a limitation that stalled instances are automatically restarted after 7 days. This ensures that instances receive security patches and maintenance updates that can only be applied with the instance in execution. If the team does not plan the RDS to save inside 7 days, the instance is restarted automatically and the billing returns to normal.

Incorrect. Automated backups of RDS do not force the restart of stalled instances — they are simply jumped during the stalled period and resumed when the instance returns to run. 7 days is the need to apply maintenance patches, not backups.

Incorrect. There is no standard behavior of the CloudWatch Restart RDS low use of CPU. Automatic restart after 7 days stopped is a behavior of the service itself RDS (documented by AWS), not an alarm CloudWatch standard.

Incorrect. Multi-AZ failover occurs when the primary instance becomes INACESSIBLE (hardware failure, AZ failure) — not simply when it is in the 'stopped' state. A stopped instance does not activate the Multi-AZ failover. 7 days is a behavior of RDS for maintenance, not Multi-AZ.

questions.text: A company uses NAT Gateway for which instances EC2 in private sub-networks access the internet. The team realized that 60% of the cost of NAT Gateway is of instances in 3 Different AZs communicating with the same NAT Gateway in a single AZ (cross-AZ traffic). How to reduce this cost by maintaining internet connectivity for private fora?
options: Replace NAT Gateway by one NAT Forum (EC2 with NAT configured) in a single central AZ — NAT Mechanisms are cheaper per hour than NAT Gateway and eliminate the cost of processing by GB
Configure VPC Endpoints for all services AWS used — with VPC Endpoints, instances access services AWS directly without passing through NAT Gateway, eliminating 100% of the cost of NAT Gateway
Enable 'Split-horizon' DNS' the VPC to redirect service requests AWS for private endpoints, reducing traffic by NAT Gateway

Create a NAT Gateway in each AZ and configure the route tables of each private sub-network to use the NAT Gateway the MESMA AZ — traffic within the same AZ between instances EC2 and NAT Gateway is free, eliminating cross-AZ cost
questions.explanation: Right. Traffic between sub-networks in the same AZ is free. By creating a NAT Gateway by AZ and configure the routes of each private sub-network to the NAT Gateway local (same AZ), all traffic of instances for the NAT Gateway is intra-AZ (free). NAT Gateway by GB still exists, but the cross-AZ transfer cost is eliminated. The cost of 3 NAT Gateways vs. 1 is offset by elimination of cross-AZ costs.
questions.hint: What is the cost of data transfer between resources in MESMA AZ? How does this change the positioning strategy of the NAT Gateway to eliminate cross-AZ collections?
optionRationales: Right. Traffic between sub-networks in the same AZ is free. By creating a NAT Gateway by AZ and configure the routes of each private sub-network to the NAT Gateway local (same AZ), all traffic of instances for the NAT Gateway is intra-AZ (free). NAT Gateway by GB still exists, but the cross-AZ transfer cost is eliminated. The cost of 3 NAT Gateways vs. 1 is offset by elimination of cross-AZ costs.

Incorrect as a solution to the cross-AZ cost problem. NAT A single AZ procedure would still cause the same cross-AZ traffic problem of instances in other AZs., NAT Mechanisms require manual management (patches, scalability, high availability), adding operational overhead. Cross-AZ transfer cost would remain.

Partially correct but not a complete solution. VPC Endpoints eliminate the need for NAT Gateway for services AWS specific (S3, DynamoDB they are free; others have an endpoint cost. However, if the instances also need access to the public internet (downloads of packages, external APIs)), VPC Endpoints do not cover this traffic — the NAT Gateway The complete solution for the cross-AZ cost is to create a NAT Gateway by AZ.

Incorrect. 'Split-horizon' DNS' (or DNS divided) in the context AWS refers to solving names of DNS for private endpoints within the VPC instead of public endpoints — what is a functionality of VPC Endpoints (Private DNS), not an independent router mechanism. It is not a solution for the cross-AZ cost of NAT Gateway.

questions.text: A company uses Amazon DynamoDB for an e-commerce application. Traffic patterns are highly variable — peaks of 10.000 RCU/s during promotions and only 100 RCU/The team wants to optimize costs without manually managing the capacity provided. DynamoDB is more economical for this highly variable traffic profile?
options: DynamoDB Provided with Auto Scaling configured with target of 70% of use — Auto Scaling automatically adjusts the capacity between 100 and 10.000 RCU/s as traffic varies

DynamoDB Provided with Reserved Capacity (Reserved Capacity Reservation by 1 or 3 years) for the 100 RCU/baseline, with On-Demand covering the additional peaks — the combination minimizes the total cost

DynamoDB On-Demand — charge for individual requests (RCU/WCU per operation) without providing capacity in advance; instantly adapts to any traffic without throttling and is more economical when traffic is unpredictable or has large variations between peaks and valleys

DynamoDB Provided with fixed capacity of 5.000 RCU/s (average between peak and valley) — balances cost and availability, paying less than provision for peak and tolerates occasional throttling at times of greatest demand
questions.explanation: Correct.. DynamoDB On-Demand does not require capacity provisioning — you pay for what you use. For highly variable traffic with peak/valley ratio of 100:1 (10.000 vs 100 RCU/s), provisioning for peak would be wasteful 99% On-Demand is generally more economical when the average use is below the average use, and provide for the average would cause throttling in peaks. ~20-30% maximum capacity.
questions.hint: For traffic with large variations (100:1 between peak and valley), which mode of DynamoDB is more economical — to pay for continuously provided capacity, or to pay only for what is consumed?
optionRationales: Correct.. DynamoDB On-Demand does not require capacity provisioning — you pay for what you use. For highly variable traffic with peak/valley ratio of 100:1 (10.000 vs 100 RCU/s), provisioning for peak would be wasteful 99% On-Demand is generally more economical when the average use is below the average use, and provide for the average would cause throttling in peaks. ~20-30% maximum capacity.

Partially correct: DynamoDB Auto Scaling adjusts the capacity provided based on use. Auto Scaling is not instantaneous (may take minutes to climb) — during abrupt peaks, throttling may occur. 100x (100 for 10.000 RCU/s), On-Demand instantly adapts without throttling and can be more economical, because Auto Scaling with a minimum capacity of 100 and maximum of 10.000 still collects by the provided capacity between scalings.

Incorrect. Provide the average between peak and valley (5.000 RCU/s) means: pay for 5.000 RCU/s continuously (much more than necessary in quiet hours of 100 RCU/s), and still have throttling in peaks of 10.000 RCU/s. On-Demand pays for real use — would be more economical in calm periods and without throttling in peaks.

Partially correct in concept (cover baseline with Reserved and overflow with On-demand), but the DynamoDB Reserved Capacity (purchase of RCU/WCU in volume with discount) DO NOT work in combination with On-Demand mode — Reserved Capacity applies only to the Provided mode. You cannot mix modes per table. For the highly variable profile described, On-Demand pure is simpler and often more economical.

questions.text: A company uses AWS Lambda Extensively. The team noticed that some functions Lambda use 3.008 MB of memory but metrics show that the actual memory use is of only 200 MB. What change reduces costs without affecting the performance of functions?
options: Reduce configured memory from Lambda for a value close to actual use (ex.: 256 MB) — Lambda charge by memory product × duration (GB-seconds), then less memory = lower cost per execution, as long as the use of real memory does not exceed the new limit
Migrate functions Lambda memory sub-used for AWS Fargate — Fargate collects only by vCPU and memory used during execution, without overhead of allocated but unused memory

Use Lambda Power Tuning to find the optimal memory size that minimizes cost × performance — Power Tuning can identify if reducing memory increases both the duration and total cost increases instead of falling
Configure Lambda with Provided Competition for underutilized functions — provided competition reduces cold start and optimizes memory usage between multiple invocations
questions.explanation: The cost of Lambda is calculated as the number of requests × (memory_GB × duration_seconds). 3.008 MB to 256 MB reduces cost in ~92% for the same duration (assuming that the function does not use more than 256 MB). It is important to check that the function uses no more memory than the new limit to avoid OOM (Out of Memory) errors.
questions.hint: The cost of Lambda It's GB-seconds (memory × duration). If memory is configured 15x above actual use, which is the most direct action to reduce cost?
optionRationales: The cost of Lambda is calculated as the number of requests × (memory_GB × duration_seconds). 3.008 MB to 256 MB reduces cost in ~92% for the same duration (assuming that the function does not use more than 256 MB). It is important to check that the function uses no more memory than the new limit to avoid OOM (Out of Memory) errors.

Incorrect as cost solution for Lambda with excessive memory. Fargate is a significant change of platform (requires containerization), ECS Task Definitions etc.) and is not necessary — simply reduce the configured memory of Lambda is the direct solution and least effort for the same result.

Correct as an optimization tool, but more complex than what is needed for this scenario. 200 MB and memory is in 3.008 MB, simply reduce to 256-512 MB (leaving margin) is obvious and effective — does not require Power Tuning for this decision. Power Tuning is more useful to find the optimal size when the memory/duration/cost ratio is not obvious.

Incorrect and increased costs. Lambda Provided Competition AUMENTA the cost — you pay for instances Lambda hot kept 24/7, even when there are no invocations. It has no relation to memory usage optimization. The problem is memory CONFIGURADA excessive, not cold starters.

questions.text: A company uses Amazon CloudFront to distribute content globally. The application serves users mainly in North America and Europe, but rarely in Asia and Oceania. CloudFront is high due to the edge locations in all regions. How to reduce these costs without impacting the main users (North America and Europe)?
options: Migrate static content to a bucket S3 with S3 Transfer Acceleration — Transfer Acceleration Uses edge locations of the CloudFront for uploads but has lower cost of egress to distant regions

Configure the CloudFront Price Class — use 'Price Class' 100' (only Americas and Europe) instead of the pattern that includes all regions; users of Asia/Oceania are still served but by edge locations closer within the Price Class (with slightly higher latency), while the transfer costs are reduced by excluding the regions of highest price per GB
Use a larger cache in CloudFront (increase or TTL maximum) — objects cached for longer result in fewer requests at source and less data transfer cost
Use CloudFront Signed URLs with TTL of 24 hours — signed URLs prevent bots and scrapers from consuming the band CloudFront in high-cost regions, reducing total cost
questions.explanation: Correct.. CloudFront Price Classes allow you to select which regions of edge locations are used by the distribution. 100 includes only edge locations in the Americas and Europe — the regions with the lowest transfer cost per GB. Users from other regions will still be served by the edge locations of the selected Price Class (usually the nearest included), accepting slightly higher latency. Reduces costs excluding high-cost regions such as Asia, Oceania.
questions.hint: What configuration of the CloudFront allows you to choose which regions of edge locations are used by a distribution, excluding high-cost regions per GB when traffic in them is low?
optionRationales: Correct.. CloudFront Price Classes allow you to select which regions of edge locations are used by the distribution. 100 includes only edge locations in the Americas and Europe — the regions with the lowest transfer cost per GB. Users from other regions will still be served by the edge locations of the selected Price Class (usually the nearest included), accepting slightly higher latency. Reduces costs excluding high-cost regions such as Asia, Oceania.

Partially correct about reducing requests at source, but the cost described is from TRANSFER OF THE CLOUDFRONT PARA USERS (egress) — not transferable from origin to CloudFront. Increase TTL reduces requests to origin (reduced cost of origin fetch), but does not change the cost of serving data to end users, which depends on where they are and which ones edge locations are used.

Incorrect. S3 Transfer Acceleration is for uploads (data input to S3), not to serve content for end users. For content distribution for end users with edge region control, CloudFront Price Classes are the right mechanism. Transfer Acceleration does not replace CloudFront for distribution.

Incorrect for the cost problem described. Signed URLs control ACESSO the specific content — do not control which edge regions serve the content. Even with Signed URLs, legitimate users in Asia and Oceania would continue to use edge locations price classes is the correct mechanism for controlling regions..

questions.text: A company uses AWS Trusted Advisor and the AWS Compute Optimizer for Cost Optimization. The team wants to understand which one to use to get rightsizing recommendations (ideal size) for instances EC2 based on historical metrics of use. Which tool is best suited for rightsizing recommendations based on performance data?
options: AWS Systems Manager Inventory — Collecting configuration data from all instances EC2 and compares with industry usage references to recommend ideal sizes
AWS Cost Explorer with Rightsizing Recommendations — offers instance size recommendations based on historical cost and economic projections, without dependence on CloudWatch Metrics
AWS Trusted Advisor — analyze the environment AWS and provides detailed recommendations for rightsizing based on metrics for the use of CPU and memory of the last 14 days

AWS Computer Optimizer — Uses Machine Learning to analyze historical metrics of CloudWatch (CPU, memory via CloudWatch Agent, network I/O and disk) and recommends the type and size of instance EC2 ideal for each workload, with performance and cost estimates
questions.explanation: Correct. AWS Compute Optimizer is specifically designed for ML-based rightsizing recommendations using historical performance metrics. EC2, Lambda, ECS and volumes EBS. Provides detailed recommendations with performance justification (e.g. 'over-provided by 40% CPU, recommend m5.large instead of m5.xlarge') and estimates of economy and impact on performance.

optionRationales: Correct. AWS Compute Optimizer is specifically designed for ML-based rightsizing recommendations using historical performance metrics. EC2, Lambda, ECS and volumes EBS. Provides detailed recommendations with performance justification (e.g. 'over-provided by 40% CPU, recommend m5.large instead of m5.xlarge') and estimates of economy and impact on performance.

Partially correct: or Trusted Advisor has a check of 'Low Usage' Amazon EC2 Mechanisms' identifying instances with low use of CPU (below 10%). However, it does not provide such detailed recommendations for rightsizing based on ML as the Computer Optimizer — only alert on under-utilization. Computer Optimizer is the specific tool for detailed rightsizing recommendations.

Partially correct: Cost Explorer it has recommendations of rightsizing that consider use and cost. However, these recommendations are based on use of CPU of the CloudWatch (requires CloudWatch Memory Agent), are not as detailed in performance analysis as the Compute Optimizer that uses ML. Compute Optimizer is the dedicated tool for this type of analysis.

Incorrect. Systems Manager Inventory collects software and hardware configuration metadata (which applications are installed, versions, hardware configurations) — does not analyze performance metrics for rightsizing recommendations. Computer Optimizer is the correct tool for this analysis.

questions.text: A company needs to run a big data analysis workload that uses Apache Spark in Amazon EMR. The workload runs by 4 The Core Nodes need to be reliable (cannot be interrupted), but the Task Nodes (additional workers) can be restarted. EMR for this profile?
options: Use only Spot Instances for all nodes of the cluster EMR — o EMR automatically manages the replacement of us Spot interrupted, keeping processing without data loss
Use EMR Serverless instead of clusters EMR managed — or EMR Serverless does not have separate Master, Core and Task Nodes, charging only for processing time without managing us

Core Nodes with On-Demand or Reserved Instances (for reliability of data in HDFS) + Task Nodes with Spot Instances (for processing extra tolerant to interruption) — Spot Instances for Task Nodes reduce computing cost by up to 90% without affecting the integrity of the data in HDFS which resides in the Core Nodes
Use Spot Instances for Master Node and On-Demand for Core and Task Nodes — Master Node does not store data and can be easily replaced if interrupted
questions.explanation: That's the architecture recommended by AWS for EMR with cost-benefit: Core Nodes (hosting the HDFS and need continuity) use On-Demand or RIs, while Task Nodes (only computing, no data HDFS) can use Spot Instances If a Task Node Spot is interrupted, Spark reprocesses lost tasks using other nodes — no data loss.
questions.hint: No. EMR, which we host data in HDFS (need reliability) and what are we purely for computing (tolerated interruption)? How this distinction guides the choice of On-Demand vs. Spot?
optionRationales: That's the architecture recommended by AWS for EMR with cost-benefit: Core Nodes (hosting the HDFS and need continuity) use On-Demand or RIs, while Task Nodes (only computing, no data HDFS) can use Spot Instances If a Task Node Spot is interrupted, Spark reprocesses lost tasks using other nodes — no data loss.

Incorrect for Core Nodes. If a Core Node Spot is interrupted, HDFS may lose data blocks if replication has not been completed before interruption. EMR cannot instantly replace an interrupted Core Node without risk of data loss HDFS. Core Nodes need reliable instances (On-Demand or RIs)).

Incorrect. Master Node (NameNode of HDFS, ResourceManager of YARN) if the Master Node is interrupted, the whole cluster for — the analysis job would be lost and the cluster would need to be recreated. Master Node must be On-Demand, no Spot.

Partly correct that EMR Serverless simplifies management. However, to maximize ECONOMIA for workloads of 4 hours with Task Nodes tolerant to interruption, Spot Instances for Task Nodes can be more economical than EMR Serverless depending on usage and patterns., EMR Serverless has limitations on system configurations and custom dependencies.

questions.text: A company uses Amazon EBS and realized that it is paying for many volumes gp2. After analysis, the team discovered that most volumes have less than 1 TB and does not use the gp2 burst credits. How to migrate to gp3 would generate economy, and what is the main difference between gp2 and gp3?
options: gp3 is cheaper by GB (20% less than gp2), offers 3.000 IOPS and 125 MB/s of guaranteed baseline INDEPENDENTE volume size (gp2 binds IOPS size: 3 IOPS/Minimum GB), and allows to increase IOPS and throughput separately from volume size via configuration — migration from gp2 to gp3 reduces cost without changing performance
Migration from gp2 to gp3 requires downtime of instance EC2 and volume reformation — therefore, despite the lower cost, migration is disruptive and should be carefully planned
gp3 is only available for new instances — existing gp2 volumes cannot be converted to gp3 and need to be replaced by new volumes created as gp3
gp2 uses accumulated burst credits over time (up to 3.000 IOPS in burst) that gp3 does not have — for workloads that need burst, gp2 is superior; for stable workloads, gp3 is cheaper
questions.explanation: Right. Key differences: gp3 has price ~20% lower per GB than gp2; gp3 guarantees 3.000 IOPS and 125 MB/s shape FIXA (not dependent on size), while gp2 provides 3 IOPS/GB (small volumes have less IOPS baseline, depending on burst credits); gp3 allows to add IOPS/throughput extras independent of size. For small volumes (<334 GB) which do not use burst, gp3 is always more economical with equivalent performance or better.
questions.hint: What is the price difference between gp2 and gp3, and how the baseline of IOPS of both types behaves in relation to volume size — especially for small volumes?
optionRationales: Right. Key differences: gp3 has price ~20% lower per GB than gp2; gp3 guarantees 3.000 IOPS and 125 MB/s shape FIXA (not dependent on size), while gp2 provides 3 IOPS/GB (small volumes have less IOPS baseline, depending on burst credits); gp3 allows to add IOPS/throughput extras independent of size. For small volumes (<334 GB) which do not use burst, gp3 is always more economical with equivalent performance or better.

Incorrect. gp3 GARANTIDO has 3.000 IOPS baseline with no need for burst credits — more IOPS that a gp2 volume of up to 1 TB (that you have 3 IOPS/GB × 1000 GB = 3.000 IOPS, not counting burst). For workloads that PRECISARIAM gp2 burst (peaks above 3.000 IOPS), gp3 with IOPS extra provisions would be the solution. gp3 is equal to or better than gp2 in all cases.

Incorrect. Migration from gp2 to gp3 is done online via EBS ModifyVolume without downtime — the volume remains connected and in use during the modification, which is applied progressively. There is no need to dismantle the volume, stop the instance, or reformat the file system.
Incorrect volume EBS gp2 can be converted to gp3 using the API ModifyVolume or console AWS without creating a new volume. The volume type is modified in-place, without data loss and without downtime.

questions.text: A company is reviewing its container architecture in Amazon ECS. There are two types of workloads: batch jobs that run sporadically by 30 minutes and can be restarted if they fail, and microservices of API Rolling 24/7. From the cost point of view, what a combination of launch types ECS It's more economical.?
options: All workloads in ECS with Fargate — Fargate does not require instance management EC2, has zero cost of idleness (pays only for the execution of tasks), and is more economical than EC2 For microservices 24/7
Microservices of API no ECS Fargate with Provided Competition + Batch jobs with Lambda (no ECS) — Lambda scale to zero between executions, eliminating costs when there are no batch jobs

Microservices of API no ECS with EC2 launch type using Reserved Instances (use 24/7 predictable) + Batch jobs in ECS with Fargate Spot or EC2 Spot (Discontinuation tolerances, rotate sporadically) — RIs for continuous use and Spot for sporadic workloads is the most economical combination
All workloads in ECS with EC2 On-Demand — On-Demand offers maximum flexibility without compromise, ideal for variable traffic workloads as sporadic batch jobs
questions.explanation: Correct. Microservices 24/7 with predictable profile, EC2 with Reserved Instances offers greater discount. For sporadic batch jobs tolerant to restart, Fargate Spot (discount up 70% about Fargate) or EC2 Spot are more economical. Fargate Spot is especially suitable for batch jobs: you pay only for the duration of the execution (per second) without managing instances EC2.
questions.hint: For microservices 24/7 with predictable profile, which model of purchase offers discount per commitment? For sporadic batch jobs tolerant to interruption, which launch type ECS offers even discount 70%?
optionRationales: Correct. Microservices 24/7 with predictable profile, EC2 with Reserved Instances offers greater discount. For sporadic batch jobs tolerant to restart, Fargate Spot (discount up 70% about Fargate) or EC2 Spot are more economical. Fargate Spot is especially suitable for batch jobs: you pay only for the duration of the execution (per second) without managing instances EC2.

Partly correct that Fargate eliminates management of EC2 and charge for use, but for microservices 24/7, EC2 with Reserved Instances usually is more economical than Fargate pure (Fargate has cost per second of vCPU+memory that may be higher than RIs EC2 shared between multiple containers). For large clusters with high density of containers, EC2 with RIs is more economical than Fargate.

Incorrect as a more economical solution. On-Demand without any discount is not the most economical option for microservices 24/7 (RIs are cheaper) nor for sporadic batch jobs (Spot/Fargate Spot with up to 70-90% On-Demand offers flexibility but does not maximize economy..

Incorrect. 'Provisioned Competition' is a concept of Lambda, not ECS Fargate. In addition, Lambda has a limit of 15 minutes per run and is not suitable for batch jobs 30 The combination ECS EC2 with RIs for microservices + Fargate Spot for batch is the correct architecture for ECS.

questions.text: A company recently revised its account AWS and found multiple unused features: Elastic IP Addresses without associated instances, snapshots of EBS old, and volumes EBS which statement is correct about the collection of these resources?
options: Volumes EBS not attached to bodies do not generate collection — a AWS suspends volume collection EBS when they are disconnected (detached), resuming only when they are reattached to an instance

Elastic IPs not associated with running instances have hourly collection; snapshots EBS have collection per GB stored per month; volumes EBS non-attached also have continuous collection per GB provided — all three generate continuous costs even without active use
Snapshots EBS are free if they are kept in the same region as the volume of origin — the collection occurs only when the snapshot is copied to another region
Only Elastic IPs generate collection when not used — snapshots and volumes EBS not attached are stored free of charge by AWS as courtesy to facilitate future restoration
questions.explanation: Correct. AWS charges for allocated resources even if unused: (1) Elastic IPs DESASSOCIADOS or associated with fora PARADAS have hourly collection (~$0.005/hr); (2) Snapshots EBS are charged by stored GB/month at the rate of S3 incremental; (3) Volumes EBS are charged by GB provided/month regardless of whether they are attached to instances. These 'forgotten' resources accumulate costs over time..
questions.hint: What resources AWS generate continuous collections even when idle — no associated running instances? Think of Elastic IP, EBS Snapshot, and volume EBS non-attached.
optionRationales: Correct. AWS charges for allocated resources even if unused: (1) Elastic IPs DESASSOCIADOS or associated with fora PARADAS have hourly collection (~$0.005/hr); (2) Snapshots EBS are charged by stored GB/month at the rate of S3 incremental; (3) Volumes EBS are charged by GB provided/month regardless of whether they are attached to instances. These 'forgotten' resources accumulate costs over time..

Incorrect. Both snapshots and volumes EBS have continuous storage charges, regardless of use. Snapshots are charged for GB/month stored in S3 (incrementally), and volumes EBS provideded (gp2, gp3, io1 etc.) charge for GB/month regardless of whether they are in use.

Incorrect volume EBS are charged continuously by storage PROVISIONADO whether or not they are attached to the bodies. 'Stop' the charge of a volume EBS requires DELETAR the volume (after creating a snapshot if necessary to preserve the data)).

Incorrect. Snapshots EBS have storage charge in the same region where they were created — they do not depend on the region of the volume of origin, and there is no exemption because they are from the same region. ADICIONAIS in the destination region, but those of the original region also charge.

questions.text: A company uses Amazon S3 to store objects with varied access. For objects with more than 128 KB that have unknown access pattern, the architecture team wants to use S3 Intelligent-Tiering. However, some small objects (<1 KB) are often stored and the team wants to ensure that the Intelligent-Tiering monitoring rate does not make this option inefficient for small objects.?
options: S3 Intelligent-Tiering has no monitoring fee — it's free and can be used for any size objects at no additional cost besides storage
For objects smaller than 128 KB, the S3 Intelligent-Tiering moves them automatically to the frequent access Tier, ensuring that the monitoring rate is compensated for maximum performance

S3 Intelligent-Tiering charges a small monitoring fee per object per month — for objects smaller than 128 KB, the cost of monitoring can be proportionally higher than the tiering economy; a AWS recommends not to use Intelligent-Tiering for objects below 128 KB, preferring S3 Standard for these small objects

The monitoring rate of the Intelligent-Tiering is charged by stored GB, not by number of objects — therefore small objects cost less to monitor and are more economical in the Intelligent-Tiering than large objects
questions.explanation: Right. Intelligent-Tiering charges a tracking fee per object (~$0.0025 by 1.000 For small objects (<128 KB), the monitoring cost can be equal to or greater than the tiering economy (because small objects have low storage cost independent of the tier). AWS recommends S3 Standard for objects below 128 KB (some documents cite 128 KB as the limit from which Intelligent-Tiering becomes economically advantageous).
questions.hint: The S3 Intelligent-Tiering charges a fee per OBJETO (For very small objects, this rate may be higher than the tiering economy — what minimum size to AWS recommends using Intelligent-Tiering with economic benefit?
optionRationales: Right. Intelligent-Tiering charges a tracking fee per object (~$0.0025 by 1.000 For small objects (<128 KB), the monitoring cost can be equal to or greater than the tiering economy (because small objects have low storage cost independent of the tier). AWS recommends S3 Standard for objects below 128 KB (some documents cite 128 KB as the limit from which Intelligent-Tiering becomes economically advantageous).

Incorrect. S3 Intelligent-Tiering has a monitoring/automation rate per object stored per month. For large volumes of small objects, this rate can be significant in relation to the storage cost of the objects themselves..

Incorrect. Intelligent-Tiering moves objects based on the actual access pattern — it has no special logic that keeps small objects on the Common Access Tier. Small objects not accessed by 30 days would be moved to the Infrequent Access tier like any other object, but would still incur the monitoring rate.

Incorrect. Intelligent-Tiering's monitoring rate is by OBJETO (not by GB) — which means that many small objects can generate a cost of monitoring disproportionate to the volume of data. This makes Intelligent-Tiering less efficient for large amounts of small objects.

questions.text: A company uses AWS Organizations with Consolidated Billing. The finance team wants to understand how the discounts from Reserved Instances and Savings Plans are shared among the accounts within the organization. What statement is correct?
options: Savings Plans are specific to the account you purchased and are never shared between the organization's accounts — only Reserved Instances can be shared
Benefits of Reserved Instances are shared only between accounts in the same Organizational Unit (OU) — accounts in different OUs do not share benefits, unless explicitly configured
In order to share the benefits of RI, the buyer account needs to explicitly transfer the RI to the beneficiary account via 'Modification' on the console EC2

By default, benefits of Reserved Instances and Savings Plans are shared between TODAS the accounts of the organization via Consolidated Billing — if an account purchased an IR and is not using it, another account in the organization can automatically benefit from that discount in compatible On-Demand instances
questions.explanation: The Consolidated Billing of AWS Organizations automatically share the benefits of RIs and Savings Plans among all accounts within the organization, unless RI Sharing is explicitly disabled. This maximizes the use of discount commitments — compatible On-Demand instances in any organization account receive the discount if the buyer account is not using the commitment at that time.
questions.hint: At Consolidated Billing's Organizations, as the discounts of Reserved Instances and Savings Plans spread between accounts — what is the standard behavior when the buyer account does not use all compromised capacity?
optionRationales: The Consolidated Billing of AWS Organizations automatically share the benefits of RIs and Savings Plans among all accounts within the organization, unless RI Sharing is explicitly disabled. This maximizes the use of discount commitments — compatible On-Demand instances in any organization account receive the discount if the buyer account is not using the commitment at that time.

Incorrect. RI sharing does not have this limitation of OR — it is between TODAS the organization's accounts by default (when RI Sharing is enabled). There is no 'share between specific OOs' configuration — the scope is the entire organization.

Incorrect. Savings Plans, as well Reserved Instances, have shared benefits between organization accounts via Consolidated Billing by default. Management account can disable sharing of Savings Plans on account, but by default they are shared.

Incorrect. Sharing RI in Consolidated Billing is AUTOMATICAL — does not require transfer or modification of RIs. AWS automatically applies the IR discount from the buyer account to compatible instances in other accounts of the organization when the buyer account is not using. 'IR modification' is to change the scope, size or AZ of an IR, not to share.

questions.text: A company uses AWS Cost Explorer to analyze expenses and realized that the costs of S3 Request are very high — mainly called GetObject from a web application that makes many small frequent requests. The team wants to reduce these costs without changing the data in S3. Which solution reduces the cost of S3 Request for this application?
options: Place the Amazon CloudFront in front of the S3 as CDN — o CloudFront cache objects frequently accessed in edge locations and serves as a cache in subsequent requests, drastically reducing direct GetObject calls to S3 (S3 Request costs are charged only in the CloudFront for S3, not in cache services)
Migrate objects to S3 Express One Zone — Express One Zone has lower latency and lower cost per request than S3 Standard, being ideal for applications with many small frequent requests
Use S3 Batch Operations to consolidate multiple GetObject requests in a single batch operation — Batch Operations have low fixed cost per job regardless of the number of processed objects
Enable S3 Request Country — request costs are transferred to users who make requests, eliminating the cost to the company hosting the data
questions.explanation: Correct. CloudFront reduces the costs of S3 Request for two reasons: (1) Not cached items CloudFront are served by the edge locations no new call to S3 (cache hit = 0 requests to S3); (2) The transfer of data from CloudFront for users has different cost (usually lower) than direct transfer of S3. For web applications with many frequent requests of the same content, CloudFront can reduce the S3 requests in >90%.
questions.hint: To reduce repeated GetObject calls S3 of a web application that accesses the same objects frequently, which service reduces requests to S3 serving cache content?
optionRationales: Correct. CloudFront reduces the costs of S3 Request for two reasons: (1) Not cached items CloudFront are served by the edge locations no new call to S3 (cache hit = 0 requests to S3); (2) The transfer of data from CloudFront for users has different cost (usually lower) than direct transfer of S3. For web applications with many frequent requests of the same content, CloudFront can reduce the S3 requests in >90%.

Incorrect. S3 Batch Operations is for mass operations ASSIGNANCES (e.g. copy, delete, restore from Glacier millions of objects) — is not a mechanism to consolidate GetObject synchronous to a web application. A web application that needs real-time objects cannot use Batch Operations for this.

Partially correct on lower cost per request: S3 Express One Zone has request cost ~50% less than S3 Standard and latency single-digit ms. However, Express One Zone has cost of ARMAZENAMENTO greater than S3 Standard and is a unique AZ (less durability). In addition, for a web application with cacheable content, CloudFront is more economical — eliminates requests, not only reduces them.

Incorrect. Request Country is a model where the CLIENTE (who makes the download) pays for the request and transfer costs instead of the owner of the ticket — used for distribution of scientific/public data where the producer does not want to pay the access of consumers. For a web application where users are customers of the company, transferring the costs to them via Requester Country is not an acceptable product practice.

questions.text: Before an instance EC2 be completed by a reduction policy (scale-in) of a Auto Scaling Group, the team wants to run a script that sends pending logs to a central system and completes running connections in a graceful way — delaying the actual completion of the instance until this process ends. Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling allows you to put the instance in a waiting state before completion to execute these custom actions?
options: Health checks, configured with a longer tolerance period
Scalability policies (scaling policies) based on metrics CloudWatch
Lifecycle hooks, which place the instance in a waiting state (such as 'Terminating:Wait') before completion, allowing the execution of custom actions
Launch templates with a different startup script (user data)
questions.explanation: Correct. Lifecycle hooks pause an instance in a waiting state (e.g., 'Terminating:Wait') during launch or completion, giving time for custom scripts to run before action completes.
questions.hint: Think about the resource of Auto Scaling which puts the instance in a waiting state before being completed, giving time to perform custom actions.
optionRationales: Correct. Lifecycle hooks pause an instance in a waiting state (e.g., 'Terminating:Wait') during launch or completion, giving time for custom scripts to run before action completes.
Health checks determine whether an instance is healthy or not for replacement purposes; they do not pause the completion process for execution of custom actions.
Scalability policies decide when to add or remove instances based on metrics, but do not control what happens during the completion process of a specific instance.
Launch templates define how a new instance is configured at the time of launch (user date runs on startup) — they have no relation to actions executed before the completion of an instance.

questions.text: A company maintains a set of critical servers in its data center on-premises and wants to adopt a solution managed by AWS which continuously replicates these servers (at the disk block level) to the cloud. In case of disaster in the data center, the servers should be able to be quickly recovered as instances EC2 in a region of AWS, with the minimum possible loss of data. What service AWS it was specifically designed for this scenario?
options: AWS Snowball
AWS Direct Connect
AWS Elastic Disaster Recovery (AWS DRS)
AWS Database Migration Service (DMS)
questions.explanation: Correct. AWS Elastic Disaster Recovery continuously replicates physical, virtual or other cloud servers (at block level) to AWS, allowing rapid recovery as instances EC2 in case of disaster, with RPO of a few minutes.
questions.hint: Think of the service of AWS created specifically for continuous replication of servers as part of a disaster recovery strategy.
optionRationales: Correct. AWS Elastic Disaster Recovery continuously replicates physical, virtual or other cloud servers (at block level) to AWS, allowing rapid recovery as instances EC2 in case of disaster, with RPO of a few minutes.
The AWS DMS was designed to migrate and replicate databases between compatible sources and destinations — not to replicate entire servers at block level as part of a disaster recovery strategy.
The AWS Snowball is a physical device for mass transfer of large volumes of data (single transfer), not a continuous replication service for disaster recovery.

The AWS Direct Connect establishes a dedicated network connection between the data center and the AWS, but does not perform the continuous replication of servers or automated recovery of them by itself.

questions.text: A company stores files CSV and JSON no Amazon S3 And you want to consult them with SQL using the Amazon Athena. Before that, you need to automatically discover the schema of these files and register them as tables in a central metadata catalog. AWS Glue meets this need?
options: Glue DataBrew to infer the schema and the Amazon RDS as a catalogue
One Glue Crawler to infer the pattern and the Glue Catalog Date to record tables
One Glue Job Spark to infer the scheme and the DynamoDB as a catalogue
Glue Register scheme for cataloguing and Athena to infer the schema
questions.explanation: A) Incorrect: DataBrew is visual data preparation, and RDS does not act as a metadata catalog of the Athena. B) Correct: Crawler sweeps or S3, infer schemas and create/update tables in Glue Data Catalog — which is exactly the catalogue consulted by Athena. C) Incorrect: a Job transforms data, is not the schema discovery tool; DynamoDB is not the catalogue of Athena. D) Incorrect: the Registration Scheme versions schemas of STREAMING (Open/JSON in Kafka/Kinesis), and the Athena does not infer schema alone — he reads from Data Catalog.

questions.text: A team needs to execute transformations ETL in Spark about data on S3, sometimes a day, SEM provide or manage clusters, paying only for the job execution time. The team does not need custom low-level libraries or other frameworks beyond Spark. What service does the MENOR operational effort?
options: Amazon EMR with manually supplied clusters
Apache Spark installed in instances EC2 with Auto Scaling
AWS Glue (jobs ETL serverless)
Amazon Redshift how to store procedures
questions.explanation: A) Incorrect: EMR attends, but requires dimensioning and managing clusters — more effort than the scenario asks. B) Incorrect: managing Spark in EC2 is the scenario of MAIOR (c) Correct: Glue run Spark serverless: no cluster to create, auto scale and collect by DPU-time only during the job. D) Incorrect: Redshift is data warehouse; use stored procedures for ETL of files in S3 does not replace a managed Spark engine.

questions.text: What is the role of AWS Glue Data Catalog in a data lake architecture in AWS?
options: Physically store data processed into columnal format
Serve as a central repository of METADADOS (tables, schemas, partitions) consulted by services such as Athena, Redshift Spectrum EMR
Replace S3 as data lake storage layer
Execute queries SQL of analysts directly
questions.explanation: A) Incorrect: the data remain in the S3; the Catalog does not store data. B) Correct: the Data Catalog is the 'index' of the data lake — saves tables, schemas and partitions definitions, and is shared by Athena, Redshift Spectrum, EMR and Lake Formation. C) Incorrect: storage is the S3; the Catalog only describes what is there. D) Incorrect: who executes the queries are the engines (Athena, Spectrum); Catalog provides metadata for them.

questions.text: A company has a bank RDS PostgreSQL for the transactional system (OLTP) and needs to perform complex analytical queries with aggregations on billions of historical lines for BI reports, without impacting the transactional bank. What service is most suitable for this analytical load (OLAP)?
options: Increase the instance of RDS PostgreSQL (scale-up)
Amazon Redshift, uploading historical data to the data warehouse
Amazon ElestiCache Redis in front of the RDS
Amazon DynamoDB with global secondary indexes
questions.explanation: A) Incorrect: scale-up postpones the problem — banks OLTP are not optimized for massive analytical scans, and the IB load would continue to compete with the transactions. Redshift is the data warehouse of AWS, with columnar storage and massive parallel processing (MPP), designed exactly for aggregations over billions of lines. C) Incorrect: cache accelerates repeated readings of items, not complex analytical queries. D) Incorrect: DynamoDB is key value for OLTP high-scale; does not perform aggregations SQL analytical.

questions.text: A company keeps a cluster Amazon Redshift with the 'hot' data from the last year. Historical data from previous years (TB tens) remain in S3 in Parquet format and are consulted only occasionally, along with the cluster data. Which resource allows to consult the data of the S3 from Redshift SEM Load them in the cluster?
options: Command COPY scheduled to import everything to the cluster
Amazon Redshift Spectrum, creating an external schema pointing to the data catalog
Export cluster to S3 with UNLOAD
Amazon RDS Proxy connected to Redshift
questions.explanation: A) Incorrect: importing dozens of rarely consulted TB would force a much larger cluster — exactly the cost to be avoided. Redshift Spectrum consults data directly in S3 via external schema (using the Glue Data Catalog), allowing JOINS between cluster and cluster data S3 (c) Incorrect: UNLOAD makes the reverse path (exports results of the Redshift for the S3). D) Incorrect: RDS Proxy is pool of connections to RDS/Aurora, without relation to this scenario.

questions.text: What is the recommended way to load large volumes of data from Amazon S3 for a table of Amazon Redshift with maximum efficiency?
options: Run command COPY, which carries the files of S3 in parallel by the clusters nodes
Run individual INSERTs line-to-line from an application
Use AWS DMS in full-load mode for any load of S3
Upload files directly to the nodes disks via SSH
questions.explanation: (a) Correct: or COPY is the native and parallel method of mass loading — divides the files between the nodes and is orders of magnitude faster. B) Incorrect: INSERTs line-to-line are the classic anti-standard in Redshift, slow and expensive.: DMS is used to migrate from BANCOS of data; for files in S3 the direct path is the COPY. D) Incorrect: no access SSH to the discs of the nodes of the Redshift.

questions.text: A company ingests logs in JSON way Kinesis Date Firehose with destination in S3, for further analysis with Athena. The queries are expensive because they scan a lot of data. S3 in compressed columnar format. Which configuration resolves this SEM add components to architecture?
options: Enable S3 Transfer Acceleration to the destination pocket
Change Firehose to Kinesis Data Streams
Enable the log format conversion from Firehose itself to Apache Parquet (with schematic no Glue Catalogue Date)
Create a second function Lambda reprocessing files after delivery
questions.explanation: A) Incorrect: Transfer Acceleration accelerates uploads of distant customers, does not change the format of the data. B) Incorrect: Data Streams is raw intake; does not convert format or delivery to S3 C) Correct: Firehose has conversion NATIVA of JSON for Parquet/ORC (using a schema of the Glue Catalog) and compression — the files are already optimized for the Athena. D) Incorrect: works, but adds component and cost — the native conversion of Firehose eliminates this need.

questions.text: An event analysis architecture requires that a stream's data can be RELIDOS for new consumer applications up to 7 days after ingestion (replay), and that several consumers process the same stream independently. Which service meets these requirements?
options: Amazon Kinesis Data Streams with extended retention period
Amazon SQS Standard with DLQ
Amazon Kinesis Firehose Date
Amazon SNS with multiple entries
questions.explanation: A) Correct: Data Streams retains records (24h by standard, extendable up to 365 (b) Incorrect: no SQS the message consumed is missing from the row — there is no replay or multiple consumers of the same data. C) Incorrect: Firehose delivers and discards — does not retain stream for rereading. D) Incorrect: SNS is immediate push for subscribers; messages are not retained for later rereading.

questions.text: A company needs to calculate aggregate metrics (e.g. total sales per window of 1 minute) on a stream of the Kinesis EM TEMPO REAL, using SQL or a stream processing framework, and send the results to dashboards. Which service performs this continuous processing with time windows?
options: Amazon Athena consulting the stream directly
AWS Glue Crawler scheduled every minute
Amazon QuickSight reading the stream
Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink Kinesis Data Analytics)
questions.explanation: (a) Incorrect: Athena refer to EM data REPOUSO no S3, no streams on the move. B) Incorrect: Crawler catalog metadata; neither processes nor aggregates streams. C) Incorrect: QuickSight view data, do not process streams with windows. D) Correct: Managed Flink processes streams in real time with state and time windows (SQL/Java/Python), the case of exact use of window aggregations.

questions.text: An application consisting of API Gateway, several functions Lambda and calls to DynamoDB is with slow responses intermittently. VISUALIZAR the path of each request between the services and identify exactly which component adds latency. Which service provides this distributed tracking?
options: Amazon CloudWatch Logs Insights
AWS X-Ray, with service map and trace analysis
AWS CloudTrail
AWS Configure
questions.explanation: A) Incorrect: Logs Insights consults logs, but does not correlate the journey of a multiple-service requisition. B) Correct: X-Ray tracks end-to-end requisitions (distributed tracking), mounts the service map and shows the latency of each segment — the exact tool to find the gargalo. C) Incorrect: CloudTrail audit calls from API for governance ('who did what'), no latency of application requests. D) Incorrect: Config tracks resource configuration, no performance.

questions.text: What is the fundamental difference between Amazon CloudWatch and the AWS X-Ray in monitoring an application?
options: The CloudWatch Metric collection, logs and alarms about resources and applications; X-Ray tracks individual end-to-end requirements between services (distributed tracking))
X-Ray replaces the CloudWatch in serverless architectures
The CloudWatch is paid and X-Ray is always free
The X-Ray collects metrics of CPU and memory of the instances EC2
questions.explanation: A) Correct: they are complementary — CloudWatch responds 'how are my resources' (metrics/logs/alarms) and X-Ray responds 'where it went and where it took ESTA Incorrect: they complement each other; the X-Ray does not cover metrics or alarms. CloudWatch (with the Agent for Memory).

questions.text: A team uses the AWS X-Ray and wants to filter and group requisition traces of a specific client (e.g. search for all traces in which customer_id = '123') to investigate complaints of slowness. Which feature of X-Ray allows indexing these values for search?
options: Segment Metadata, which is automatically indexed
Annotations (annotations) added to segments, which are indexed and usable in filter expressions
CloudWatch Dashboards
Sampling rules with rate of 100%
questions.explanation: A) Incorrect: metadata is stored in the tracks but NOT indexed — not used for search filter. B) Correct: annotations are key-value pairs INDEXADOS by X-Ray, exactly to filter/group traces (e.g. annotation.customer_id = "123"). C) Incorrect: dashboards display metrics; do not filter traces by business attribute. D) Incorrect: sampling defines QUANTAS requests are tracked, not how to fetch them.

questions.text: An application in AWS Elastic Beanstalk needs to receive new versions SEM downtime and SEM reduce the capacity available during deployment; in case of failure, rollback should be fast and safe. The temporary cost of doubling instances during deployment is acceptable. Which deployment policy best meets these requirements?
options: At eleven
Rolling
Immutable
Rolling with additional batch
questions.explanation: A) Incorrect: All at once drops and updates all instances together — downtime cause. B) Incorrect: Rolling updates in batches, REDUZINDO the capacity available during the deployment. C) Correct: Immutable creates a new complete set of instances with the new version in parallel; only change when healthy — total capacity maintained and fast rollback (just discard the new ones). D) Incorrect: maintains capacity, but old instances are updated in place — slower and more risky rollback than Immutable.

questions.text: A team wants to test a new version of the application in Elastic Beanstalk in a separate environment identical to that of production and, after validating, promote the new version by exchanging traffic almost instantly, with the possibility of reversing at the same speed. Elastic Beanstalk implements this blue/green pattern?
options: Configure Rolling deployment with batch 100%
Use the 'Swap environment URLs' feature between the blue and green environments
Enable the Managed Platform Updates
Reimplant previous version by console
questions.explanation: A) Incorrect: rolling with batch of 100% is equal to all-at-once in the same environment — it is not blue/green. B) Correct: Beanstalk allows you to clone the environment, deploy the new version in the clone (green) and exchange URLs/CNAME Incorrect: Managed Platform Updates updates the PLATAFORMA (SO/runtime), no application versions. D) Incorrect: Reimplanting the previous version is slow rollback, not the blue/green pattern requested.

questions.text: A web application in Elastic Beanstalk needs to perform long tasks (image processing) without blocking requests HTTP The team wants Beanstalk to also manage the infrastructure of these tasks in the background. Elastic Beanstalk offers for this?
options: Increase the timeout of ALB to wait for processing
Create a Worker Environment, which consumes tasks from a row Amazon SQS managed by Beanstalk
Move processing to edge functions with CloudFront Functions
Use instances Spot in the same web environment
questions.explanation: A) Incorrect: arresting the request HTTP Waiting for processing is anti-standard — degrades the experience and bursts timeouts.B) Correct: Beanstalk has the Tier 'Worker Environment': the Web Tier sends the task to a queue SQS and the worker processes in background, with daemon managed by Beanstalk himself. C) Incorrect: CloudFront Functions run milliseconds of logic on the edge — unfeasible for image processing. D) Incorrect: Spot changes the purchase model, does not solve the coupling between requisition and processing.

questions.text: In which scenario the Amazon MQ is preferable to Amazon SQS/SNS?
options: When the application is new (greenfield) and born in the cloud, searching for almost unlimited scale
When an existing application depends on standard messaging protocols (JMS, AMQP, MQTT, STOMP) and the goal is to migrate without rewriting the message layer
When fan-out is needed for millions of subscribers
When the requirement is serverless queue with unlimited throughput
questions.explanation: A) Incorrect: for new applications in the cloud, the same AWS recommends SQS/SNS (serverless, larger scale, lower operational cost). Amazon MQ exists for compatibility — managed ActiveMQ/RabbitMQ brokers that speak standard protocols, allowing you to migrate legacy applications without changing code. C) Incorrect: massive fan-out is the territory of SNS. D) Incorrect: the MQ is based on brokers with defined capacity, not an unlimited serverless row.

questions.text: A company will implement the Amazon MQ (ActiveMQ) for a critical application and requires that the broker remain available even with the failure of a Availability Zone. What configuration ensures this?
options: A single instance broker with daily backups
Two independent brokers in different regions with DNS manual
Active/standby broker implemented in multiple AZs, with automatic failover
Increase the size of the single broker instance
questions.explanation: A) Incorrect: single instance in an AZ is exactly the single point of failure that you want to eliminate. B) Incorrect: independent brokers without state replication and with DNS manual do not give automatic failover or consistency. Amazon MQ offers active deployment/standby multi-AZ: if active broker AZ fails, standby automatically assumes. D) Incorrect: higher instance improves capacity, not availability.

questions.text: A financial institution requires that cryptographic keys used in AWS stay in validated hardware FIPS 140-2 Level 3, of single-tenant tenant with sole control of the institution — neither AWS which service meets this compliance requirement?
options: AWS KMS with keys managed by AWS
AWS Secrets Manager
AWS CloudHSM
AWS Certificate Manager (ACM)
questions.explanation: (a) Incorrect: KMS standard uses multi-tenant HSMs (level validation) 2 mostly, with operation managed by AWS) — does not answer 'single-tenant with exclusive control'.: Secrets Manager keep secrets (signs/credential), not a HSM. (c) Correct: or CloudHSM provides dedicated HSMs of single tenant, FIPS 140-2 Level 3, in which only the customer possesses and controls the keys. D) Incorrect: ACM certified management TLS, non-cryptographic hardware modules.

questions.text: A company wants to continue using the native integration of AWS KMS with the services of the AWS (S3, EBS, RDS), but it needs that the key material resides in dedicated HSMs under its control, by regulatory requirement. What resource combines the two worlds?
options: KMS multi-region keys
AWS KMS Custom Key Store, supported in a cluster AWS CloudHSM
Asymmetrical keys of the KMS
AWS Sign
questions.explanation: A) Incorrect: multi-Region keys replicate keys between regions — do not change where the key material resides. B) Correct: Custom Key Store connects the KMS to a cluster CloudHSM customer: services continue to use the API of the KMS, but the keys live in the dedicated HSMs. C) Incorrect: asymmetric keys change the type of encryption, not the residence of the material. D) Incorrect: Signer is for code signature, without relation to the requirement.

questions.text: A company needs to decide between transferring 80 TB by the internet (dedicated link of 500 Mbps, usable ~50% for this task) or use a AWS Snowball Edge (total time limit) ~1 the week between shipment, copy and return). 80 TB a 250 Effective Mbps take about 30 days, what is the recommendation and the main criterion?
options: Internet, because dedicated links are always more reliable
DataSync on the internet, because it compresses the data and would reduce the deadline to hours
Snowball Edge, because when the network transfer would take more than ~1 week, the physical device tends to be faster and cheaper
Split data into several bucks to speed up the link
questions.explanation: A) Incorrect: reliability does not change the band's mathematics — 30 days against 1 week. B) Incorrect: DataSync optimizes and parallels, but does not perform miracle with the physical band; compression does not reduce 30 days to hours. C) Correct: the pocket rule of the AWS: if the network transfer takes more than ~1 week, use the Snow family — 80 TB fit in a single Snowball Edge. D) Incorrect: split into buckets does not increase the available band of the link.

questions.text: What is the central difference between AWS DataSync and the AWS Storage Gateway?
options: DataSync is for TRANSFERIR/migrate data (one-time or scheduled) between on-premises and AWS; Storage Gateway provides CONTINU HYBRID access, with local cache and cloud data
Storage Gateway transfer faster than the DataSync in any scenario
DataSync only works with relational databases
They are the same service with names from different generations
questions.explanation: A) Correct: this is the classic distinction of proof — DataSync moves data from A to B (with integrity check and scheduling); Storage Gateway integrates the cloud datacenter permanently (File/Volume/Tape Gateway with local cache). B) Incorrect: they are different purposes; speed is not the criterion of choice. C) Incorrect: DataSync transfer ARQUIVOS/objects (NFS, SMB, HDFS, S3, EFS, FSx); banks are the territory of DMS. D) Incorrect: separate and complementary services.

questions.text: A company makes corporate backups in physical tapes (tape library) with legacy software and wants to eliminate the management of physical tapes and transport to external vaults, maintaining the same backup software. AWS replace the tapes with the minimum of changes?
options: Migrate all backups to the Amazon EBS
AWS Storage Gateway — Tape Gateway, featuring a VTL (Virtual Tape Library) to backup software, with virtual tapes in S3/S3 Glacier
AWS Backup with centralized plans
Amazon FSx for Windows File Server
questions.explanation: A) Incorrect: EBS is block disk for EC2 — expensive and inadequate for backup archiving. questions.text: Business partners send files daily via SFTP. The company wants to receive these files directly in a pocket S3, maintaining the protocol SFTP for partners (without changing anything), without managing servers. Which service meets this scenario?

questions.text: A company will migrate to the AWS a Windows server file that uses the protocol SMB and is integrated with Microsoft Active Directory (permissions) NTFS, DFS). Windows applications should continue to access sharing without change. Which storage service is appropriate?

questions.text: A media producer in a metropolis SEM Region AWS next needs to run virtual workstations and latency rendering of few milliseconds for your local artists, using the services and standard APIs of AWS, without installing hardware in the office itself. Which infrastructure option solves?

questions.text: With remote work, employees of a company need to access, from their notebooks and anywhere, internal applications hosted in private sub-networks of a VPC — with encrypted connection (TLS) and authentication integrated into the corporate directory. What service provides this access?

questions.text: A web application in a single instance EC2 in a single AZ suffers unavailability when the instance fails. DUAS Do combined actions make architecture highly available? (Select DUAS alternatives)

C) Correct: the ALB monitors health and distributes traffic only to healthy instances between AZs — the classic pair ALB + ASG multi-AZ. D) Incorrect: AMI accelerates manual recovery, but does not prevent unavailability. E) Incorrect: the public subnet does not change availability.

questions.text: A company needs to ensure that the objects of a pocket S3 are encrypted at rest with auditable keys and that TODO access to the pocket occurs only by encrypted connections. DUAS do settings implement these requirements? (Select DUAS alternatives)

D) Incorrect: Transfer Acceleration accelerates uploads, is not security control. E) Incorrect: tags organize and rate costs; do not apply controls..

questions.text: Two microservices communicate by calls HTTP direct synchronous: when processing service is slow or unavailable, customer requests are lost. questions.text: A Bucket S3 build up application logs: the first 30 days are frequently consulted; up to 90 days, rarely; after that, almost never — but they need to be retained by 5 years for compliance, at the lowest cost. D) Incorrect: replication DUPLICA (e) Incorrect: One Zone-IA has less resilience and minimal recovery of 30 days; does not meet the initial frequent access nor is it the cheapest class for the long term.

questions.text: A bank RDS MySQL suffers with slowness caused by (1) heavy reading reports carried out on business hours, and (2) identical repetitive consultations of a product catalogue. DUAS Do solutions attack each cause, respectively? (Select DUAS alternatives)

questions.text: Courts EC2 in private sub-networks (without NAT and without IGW) need access DOIS destinations without going through the internet: (1) Buckets S3 and (2) a API of the AWS Secrets Manager. Which ones DOIS types of VPC Should Endpoint be used, respectively? (Select DUAS alternatives)

questions.text: After an incident, a company wants to strengthen the security of the account AWS: (1) prevent the unprotected use of the root user; and (2) register TODAS calls from API of all the organization's accounts for audit. DUAS do measures implement these points? (Select DUAS alternatives)

questions.text: A stream of the Kinesis Data Streams in Provisioned Mode presents ProvidedThroughputExceededException errors in producers at peak times, and the load is unpredictable. DUAS Do actions solve the problem? (Select DUAS alternatives)
